title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon, topping AI benchmarks with cybersecurity gains
content:
Google has released Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier model, which the company states offers significant gains in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity. In a Wednesday announcement, Google highlighted that Carbon secured the top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark, outperforming Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. The new model provides improvements over Argon, which Google released earlier this month.

Currently available only to a select group of cybersecurity defense companies, Gemini 4 Carbon is slated to expand to other partners within Google’s Fairwind Program. The release reflects the pace at which Google is pushing its capabilities in these areas.
summary: Google has released its latest frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, which achieves the top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark. The model is currently available to a select group of cybersecurity defense companies before expanding to other partners in the Fairwind Program.
author: The Verge

title: Apple charges $14,549 for fully specced touchscreen MacBook Pro
content:
Apple announced a new MacBook Pro featuring an OLED display and touchscreen capabilities, positioning it at a higher price point than the model released earlier this year. The base 14-inch model starts at $2,899, while the 16-inch version begins at $3,399. However, selecting every available premium hardware option increases the cost significantly, resulting in final prices of $14,249 for the 14-inch and $14,549 for the 16-inch configurations.

These top-tier setups include the M5 Max chip with an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU, along with $150 worth of nano-texture glass. The configurations also feature 128GB of memory, which adds $2,000 to the base price, and 16TB of storage, a component identified as a major cost factor in the overall price increase.
summary: Apple’s fully specced 16‑inch MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen and M5 Max chip costs $14,549. The 14‑inch version costs $14,249, and both configurations include 128 GB of memory and 16 TB of storage.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft posts $92.3B revenue in Q1, splits report into two new segments
content:
Microsoft reported its first quarter of fiscal year 2027 results, generating $92.3 billion in revenue and $33.6 billion in net income. The company noted a 19 percent increase in revenue and a 32 percent rise in net income compared to the previous period. This financial report marks a significant shift in how Microsoft presents its data, as the company is overhauling its reporting structure for the new fiscal year.

For the first time, Microsoft has split its operations into two distinct segments: Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer. This change replaces the previous three-segment structure, which included Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. The new Agents and Infra segment encompasses businesses such as Azure.
summary: Microsoft posts $92.3B revenue in Q1, splits report into two new segments.
author: The Verge

title: Readwise Books launches beta to challenge Kindle and Kobo
content:
Readwise Books, a new platform for buying, reading, and discussing books, is currently in beta. The product expands the Readwise ecosystem, which already includes tools for storing Kindle highlights and reading saved newsletters and web articles. Access to the beta version is restricted to invitees or existing Readwise subscribers.

The launch represents a broader approach to reading than typical ebook services. Tristan Homsi and Daniel Doyon, associated with Readwise, are involved with the project.

title: Akai MPC Sample Key to feature open-source firmware and vibe-coded mods
content:
Akai is preparing to release the MPC Sample Key, a device that features a traditional keyboard layout instead of the pads found on the MPC Sample. Although the product has not yet been formally announced, the company is already showcasing custom modifications created by the modding community using vibe coding. To support this ecosystem, Akai is providing early access to the device for hackers and custom firmware developers.

The MPC Sample Key will feature open-source firmware, likely running a version of the software found on the MPC Sample with adjustments for the keyboard, pitch, and mod wheels. Unlike the higher-end MPC Key 37, the Sample Key does not include pads; users will play back samples directly using the keys.
summary: Akai is providing the modding community with early access to the MPC Sample Key, which will run open-source firmware. The device uses keys to play back samples instead of pads and includes traditional keyboard, pitch, and mod wheels.

title: St. Lucie County Won't Investigate Ownership of Unpermitted Flock Cameras
content:
St. Lucie County officials have stated they will not investigate the ownership of a cluster of unpermitted Flock cameras that were removed during a countywide takedown effort. According to a report by The Washington Post, residents remain upset because they do not know who installed the devices or how the collected data was used. Hannah Galindo, a 31-year-old resident who petitioned for the cameras' removal, expressed concern that the data could be located anywhere.

The Post reported that of the twelve cameras discovered, five were claimed by city law enforcement. A Flock spokesperson told the publication that a police department mistakenly issued guidance allowing officers to post multiple cameras under a single permit, despite the county’s requirement for individual permits. Neither Flock nor the police departments in Port St. Lucie and Fort Pierce, which claimed the cameras, will confirm who provided that guidance.
summary: St. Lucie County will not investigate who installed 12 unpermitted Flock cameras that were removed during a countywide takedown, and the cameras have since disappeared. Residents remain upset, and five cameras were claimed by city law enforcement, while a police department mistakenly issued guidance that officers could post multiple cameras under one permit.

title: Google AI Gives Evasive Answers to 2020 Election Winner Question
content:
Google’s AI Mode has begun providing indirect responses to questions regarding the outcomes of the 2020 and 2024 United States presidential elections. When asked directly who won the 2020 election, the AI advised users to consult the Federal Election Commission (FEC) for official results, statistics, and winner certification, rather than naming the victor. Similar evasive answers were received for inquiries about the 2024 election, where the AI again directed users to the FEC for information.

In contrast, the AI provided a direct link to The American Presidency Project’s 2012 Data Center when asked about the 2012 election. For every other presidential election going back to 2000, the system offered detailed and correct responses identifying the winner. These observations follow reports of complaints on social media regarding the AI’s cagey answers to these specific recent electoral queries.
summary: If you ask some prominent US politicians who won the 2020 presidential election, you might get some weasely answers that fail to directly acknowledge Joe Biden's win that November. If you ask Google's AI Mode the same question, you might get an evasive answer that simply tells you to consult with outside sources.

title: Cadillac Escalade IQ delivers 440‑mile range and 200‑kWh battery
content:
The Cadillac Escalade IQ, a large electric SUV, features a substantial battery pack containing over 200 kWh of lithium-ion cells. This capacity supports an impressive range, with Cadillac stating the vehicle achieves 460 miles (740 km) on the EPA test cycle. During a recent review, the vehicle arrived with an indicated range of 440 miles (708 km), a figure that made recharging unnecessary for a full week of testing. The model is designed to demonstrate that replacing a V8 engine with powerful electric motors does not compromise Cadillac’s ambitions, even as the brand plans to maintain a mix of electric and combustion vehicles beyond 2030.

The Escalade IQ shares its battery pack and other components with several other full-size General Motors electric vehicles, including the Chevrolet Silverado EV, the GMC Sierra EV, and the Hummer EVs. Like these models, the Escalade is characterized by its significant size and weight. Its curb weight is 9,046 lb (4,103 kg), which is approximately one-third heavier than the last gas-powered version tested. This mass places the vehicle in the Class 3 truck category, necessitating flat side mirrors and meaning there is no formal EPA range rating, despite the manufacturer’s claimed figures.

Despite the vehicle’s substantial weight, which exceeds four tons, it is equipped with numerous airbags. The Escalade is designed to be just small enough to fit into a standard parking space, balancing its large physical footprint with practical parking dimensions. The review highlights that the electric SUV’s primary advantage lies in its extensive range and the technological parity it shares with other GM full-size electric trucks and SUVs.
summary: Cadillac Escalade IQ delivers 440‑mile range and 200‑kWh battery.

title: Amazon Adds Camera to Echo Studio Smart Speaker
content:

Both versions of the Echo Studio feature a 3.75‑inch high‑excursion woofer, three full‑range drivers, Dolby Atmos support, and Amazon’s proprietary surround‑sound algorithm. They also provide lossless HD audio, Advanced Room Adaptation—which continuously tunes sound to a room’s acoustics— and noise‑distortion‑fighting features. Each unit houses a four‑mic array and the AZ3 Pro processor, which includes an AI accelerator for Amazon’s Alexa+ generative‑AI chatbot.

The primary new differentiator for the Echo Studio with Home Camera is the added camera, while its audio capabilities remain unchanged from the standard Echo Studio.

The Chrome team adds that Carbon is ten times better at producing high‑quality patches than non‑Google models.

Google also reports that Carbon has raised its score by 89 points on WebDev Arena, moving it to fourth place on the leaderboard. The model is not yet available for public use.

title: Blue Origin, SpaceX, Virgin Galactic All Pause US Space Tourism Missions
content: The private space tourism era looked so very promising five years ago. Blue Origin and Virgin Galactic had begun flying customers—real people with zero space experience—on suborbital missions. And at about the same time, private citizens were going to orbit for days at a time aboard SpaceX's Crew Dragon. But that was then. Consider the state of play today: It has been 10 months since Blue Origin's New Shepard spacecraft flew its last mission in January. The program was subsequently "paused," but let's be real. Blue Origin has moved on. New Shepard's engineering teams are now supporting the New Glenn rocket and Blue Moon lander programs. SpaceX flew its final free-flyer mission on Dragon, Fram2, in April 2025. A handful of non-NASA missions bound for space stations remain on the spacecraft's manifest, but all are likely to carry at least one government astronaut. Then Dragon will be retired. There is no credible timeline for SpaceX's Starship to fly humans into space from Earth. As for Virgin Galactic, the company flew its final suborbital mission on the VSS Unity spacecraft more than two years ago, in June 2024. So we are now 10 months, and counting, without a space tourism mission in the United States. Read full article Comments
summary: Blue Origin's New Shepard last flew in January and has been paused, while SpaceX's Dragon finished its final free‑flyer mission in April 2025 and will be retired. Virgin Galactic's final suborbital flight on VSS Unity occurred in June 2024, leaving the United States without a space tourism mission for 10 months.

title: Trump Administration Sues Utah to Protect Kalshi from State Gambling Ban
content: The Trump administration is trying to stop Utah from enforcing its gambling ban against Kalshi, making Utah the 10th state sued by the US government agency that regulates prediction markets. Utah, which prohibits gambling, sued Kalshi in a state court last week. Utah's lawsuit seeks an order prohibiting Kalshi from offering bets on sports, elections, politics, and other events. “Kalshi runs an online casino in Utah and calls it a prediction market. That violates Utah law,” Utah Attorney General Derek Brown, a Republican, said last week. “Not only do our state laws ban gambling but Utah is one of only two states where gambling is also prohibited under the state constitution. For 130 years, Utah has been clear: gambling has no place here, and we will enforce our laws.” Read full article Comments
summary: The Trump administration is suing Utah to stop the state from enforcing its gambling ban against Kalshi, making Utah the 10th state sued by the agency that regulates prediction markets. Utah sued Kalshi in state court last week, seeking an order prohibiting Kalshi from offering bets on sports, elections, politics, and other events.

title: Bush Heritage raises $19m to buy Wooroora station in far north Queensland
content:
A conservation fundraiser has secured more than $19 million in private donations to enable Bush Heritage to purchase Wooroora Station in far north Queensland. The group aims to complete the acquisition by Christmas, protecting a tract of land that connects wet tropics and World Heritage rainforest and contains headwaters that flow toward the Great Barrier Reef.

Wooroora spans over 20,000 hectares of largely intact wet sclerophyll forest and savanna woodland on the lands of the Jirrbal people, roughly 100 km south‑west of Cairns. The property borders Bush Heritage’s existing 43,575‑hectare Yourka Reserve and provides habitat for 12 endangered species, reinforcing the biodiversity of one of Australia’s most species‑rich regions.

title: US military releases clear photo of China's Shenlong space plane docked in orbit
content:
A U.S. military intelligence agency has released a new photograph of China’s reusable Shenlong space plane, capturing the spacecraft while it is docked to another satellite in orbit. The image was captured in 2024 by Vantor’s WorldView 3 satellite from a distance of 56 miles (90 kilometers). This satellite-based perspective provides a resolution of 4.5 centimeters (1.8 inches) per pixel, revealing details with greater clarity than previous ground-based observations of the spacecraft.

In the released image, the robotic Shenlong space plane is shown docked to an unidentified satellite that has its solar panels deployed. The photograph also shows Shenlong’s payload bay doors in an open position. Analysts suggest these open doors may provide clues regarding the activities of the space plane during its fourth mission, which launched in February 2026. While the specific satellite it was docked to remains unknown, the high-definition view offers new insights into the mysterious spacecraft.

China’s space agency has provided limited public information, stating only that Shenlong assists in testing technologies intended to pave the way for more convenient and affordable round-trip methods for the peaceful use of space. However, independent observations indicate the spacecraft has engaged in other activities while in orbit. In June 2026, American space intelligence company LeoLabs reported detecting a new object in the vicinity of the space plane. LeoLabs stated with high confidence that the object was released from the Chinese space plane, noting that this activity is consistent with sub-satellite deployments observed during previous missions.

Similar object releases occurred during Shenlong’s third mission, which ended in 2024, and its second mission in 2023. During the 2023 mission, the space plane may also have conducted proximity and rendezvous operations, where two spacecraft maneuver close to one another. It remains possible that the released objects were unnecessary hardware discarded before landing. Due to the military nature of the program, few operational details about Shenlong have been made public.

The United States also operates a secretive robotic space plane, the Boeing-built X-37B, and rarely releases concrete details about its capabilities or missions. In February 2025, the U.S. Space Force released its first photo of the X-37B in space, which appeared to show the craft in high Earth orbit with its payload bay doors open. Additionally, in 2023, the Space Force released an official painting depicting an X-37B-like space plane in orbit intercepting another satellite.

As China and the United States compete in what many observers describe as a new Space Race, these rare images may serve as a method for militaries and intelligence agencies to hint at their capabilities without fully disclosing them to the public.
summary: A US military intelligence agency released a high-resolution satellite image showing China's Shenlong space plane docked to another spacecraft with its payload bay doors open. The photograph, captured in 2024 by Vantor's WorldView 3 satellite, provides new details on the vehicle's fourth mission and its ability to release objects in orbit.

title: Everest: The Other Side review – couple’s climb on the mountain’s toughest face comes with tricky moral questions over their lofty ambitions
content:
National Geographic’s documentary "Everest: The Other Side" offers an immersive portrait of mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson as they attempt to become the first people to ski down Mount Everest’s north face. With some screenings presented in the IMAX format, the film is described as evoking the spectacle and scale of early large-format cinema, though its intense focus on the climbers’ ascent and descent may provoke anxiety or vertigo for some viewers.

The narrative follows Morrison and Nelson as they plan and execute practice runs for their ambitious goal. The review notes that the film spends considerable time depicting the pair scaling the steep, less-traveled north face before skiing back down, a sequence that leaves the specific motivations for the descent inadequately explained. Morrison is characterized as an amiable experienced mountaineer who appears compelled to place himself in grave danger, a risk that could potentially endanger others involved in any necessary rescue efforts.

Hilaree Nelson shares her partner’s passion for the climb, and the first third of the film tracks their preparation for the expedition. The review highlights that neither climber seems able to fully articulate why they have chosen to take such significant risks. Nelson attempts to frame her mountaineering lifestyle as a personal career choice that her two teenage sons should accept, suggesting they might even thank her for it. This perspective is complicated by the reality that if she were injured or lost, her sons and Morrison—who is not the boys’ biological father—would be left to deal with the aftermath.
summary: The documentary follows mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson as they seek to become the first people to ski down Everest's north face. The film presents an immersive portrait of their climb while raising moral questions about their risky ambitions and the potential impact on their family.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Metropolis: Street Photography 1985–2025 exhibition opens in Sydney
content:
The exhibition Metropolis: Street Photography 1985–2025 is currently on display at The Photographic Gallery in Sydney, running until 17 November. The collection documents over four decades of urban life, transitioning from the film-noir streets of 1980s New York to the period surrounding the fall of the Berlin Wall. It concludes with the modern, colour-saturated geometry of contemporary Australian streets, showcasing a range from classic monochrome grit to vivid colour abstraction.

The exhibition examines how photographers have captured the relentless energy of ever-changing cities. It serves as a celebration of unscripted characters, strange encounters, and the absurd comedy that emerges when people share public space.
summary: The exhibition spans four decades of street photography, transitioning from 1980s New York film-noir styles to contemporary Australian colour imagery. It showcases how photographers have documented the energy and characters of changing cities until 17 November at The Photographic Gallery, Sydney.

content:

The new feature is a darkly comic western loosely based on Nikolai Gogol’s 1842 novel of the same name. Cox invites fans to submit questions about the project and his career.

title: Peven Everett documentary explores life after cancer and musical career
content: A new documentary follows the Chicagoan from child trumpet prodigy to Gabriel-singing icon and DIY maverick. ‘Not everybody wants to see musical genius’, he says At We Out Here festival in Dorset in August, thousands of people could be heard singing a trumpet melody as if it was a giant brass-band karaoke session. On stage was Peven Everett, performing a rendition of Gabriel, one of the most celebrated anthems in dance-music history. Co-created with producer Roy Davis Jr, the best-known version, which blew up in UK clubs in the mid-90s, is a spiritual garage-house track about the “archangel of love” that can bring both punters and DJs to tears. But Everett is much more than one song. Damon Albarn of Gorillaz tells me that “Peven has a once-in-a-generation voice … he’s a great inspiration to us all.” We Out Here founder, Gilles Peterson says that the Chicagoan is, alongside Detroit’s Moodymann and Amp Fiddler, “the closest thing dance music has to a Prince-type figure”. A prolific multi-instrumentalist and one-man cottage industry, Everett’s catalogue spans more than 500 tracks, across house, neo-soul, hip-hop, samba and more.
summary: A new documentary follows Chicagoan Peven Everett from child trumpet prodigy to house music icon and DIY maverick. The film examines his life after cancer and his role in vanquishing the 'Disco Sucks' movement.

title: Horror plays from London take over New York stage amid demand for communal experiences
content:
Horror productions are currently dominating the New York stage, driven by a surge in demand for communal experiences. Hit London plays, including 2:22, Paranormal Activity, and A Ghost in Your Ear, are now performing on and off Broadway. This trend coincides with a broader post-pandemic shift as audiences seek to escape smartphone addiction and return to in-person interactions.

The recovery of the entertainment industry supports this shift toward live, immersive events. Hollywood and Broadway box office revenues have returned to pre-pandemic levels this year, while IMAX and 4DX formats are breaking records. Additionally, concert attendance has reached new highs, and the most recently tracked season of New York theatre grossed more than the previous one. Consequently, horror, described as the most communal genre, has become the hottest ticket for the fall.
summary: Successful London productions including 2:22, Paranormal Activity, and A Ghost in Your Ear are now drawing large audiences in New York. This surge in demand for horror theater is attributed to a post-pandemic craving for in-person communal experiences.

title: Qwan'tez Stiggers: From delivery driver to New York Jets player after father's death
content:
Qwan’tez Stiggers, a player for the New York Jets, recently shared his journey from working as a delivery driver to reaching the NFL. Stiggers’ football aspirations were derailed when he was 18, just days after arriving at college. Following a car crash that left him in a coma, his father died seven months later. Forced to drop out of school, Stiggers returned home to support his mother, Kwanna, and their 12 siblings.

During this difficult period, Stiggers’ then-girlfriend, Cheyenne, was also coping with the loss of her teenage sister to a stray bullet. For the next six years, the couple supported each other while Stiggers worked late-night delivery jobs and washed trucks to pay the bills. Although watching his former teammates advance in their football careers was challenging, Stiggers stated that he wanted better for himself while raising a child and living with his partner. Despite these hardships, he eventually realized his dream of playing in the NFL.
summary: Qwan'tez Stiggers dropped out of college to support his mother and 12 siblings after his father died. He worked as a delivery driver before eventually joining the New York Jets.

title: Marco Jansen's all-round excellence highlights lack of equivalent players in England and Australia
content:
South African cricketer Marco Jansen is highlighted as a standout all-rounder who embodies a rare combination of physical and technical attributes. Standing 6ft 8in, he possesses long limbs and a whiplash action that generates steep bounce, complemented by speed and the ability to move both ways. His left-arm delivery provides a distinct advantage, while his batting style allows him to hit sixes or adjust his approach when an innings becomes difficult. The article suggests that England and Australia are currently searching for an equivalent player to Jansen.

In the third Test, Jansen had recorded 99 Test wickets at an average of 20.81. His performance in the second Test against Australia at Gqeberha was pivotal, where he scored 85 runs to help South Africa recover from a score of 110 for six. This counterattack enabled the team to convert a precarious position into an innings victory. Although Jansen is still developing as a batter, his average of 25.66 prior to the current Test is considered an understatement of his potential.
summary: Marco Jansen, a 6ft 8in South African, has taken 99 Test wickets at 20.81 and scored 85 in the second Test against Australia. His performance demonstrates a rare combination of bowling and batting skills that England and Australia are currently seeking to replicate.

title: Mark Carney centralizes power and cuts rights laws despite global praise
content:
Shiri Pasternak, an associate professor of criminology at Toronto Metropolitan University, argues that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is facing a dual reality. Internationally, Carney is celebrated as a hero for his Davos speech, which addressed the shifting global power dynamics occurring in the shadow of Donald Trump’s presidency.

However, Pasternak contends that Carney’s domestic actions contradict this international image. She states that the Prime Minister is mirroring the US president by radically centralizing power within his office and cabinet. According to Pasternak, Carney is also dismantling dozens of laws that protect environmental, Indigenous, and labour rights to facilitate his economic agenda. Pasternak, who is also a member of the Infrastructure Beyond Extractivism research team, highlights this contrast between Carney’s external diplomatic stance and his internal political maneuvers.
summary: Mark Carney is celebrated internationally for his Davos speech addressing the reconfiguration of power under Donald Trump. content:
Most students of Renaissance art first encounter Giorgio Vasari through his book Lives of the Most Excellent Painters, Sculptors, and Architects. It has shaped how generations have understood artists such as Michelangelo, Leonardo da Vinci, and Raphael.

title: You Can See Everything review: Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes film is absurd but captivating
content:
The documentary You Can See Everything, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, is set for release in the US now and in the UK on 20 November. The film follows Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced founder of Theranos, during her final weeks before surrendering to federal prison. Fielder, a comedian known for creating elaborate scenarios with real people, moves in with Holmes, her partner Billy Evans, and their two children for the month leading up to her incarceration.

Holmes faces more than a decade in prison for falsely claiming that Theranos’s machine could perform hundreds of diagnostic tests using a single drop of blood, which defrauded investors of hundreds of millions of dollars. Despite these charges, Holmes maintains her innocence, telling Fielder she has nothing to hide and claiming she has not told a lie since childhood. However, the film suggests that her assertion that viewers can "see everything" is not accurate, as discrepancies become increasingly apparent throughout the narrative.

The film shifts its focus from Holmes to an examination of how people form perceptions of others, casting doubt on the objective recall of information, particularly when personal and professional boundaries blur. The reviewer notes that the film is difficult to categorize strictly as a documentary because Fielder appears more focused on entertainment than truth-seeking, making it hard to trust any character on screen, including Fielder himself.

Despite its absurd premise and questionable reliability, the film is described as captivating. The reviewer was engaged for almost the entire three-hour runtime, noting that Holmes ultimately "cracks" Fielder rather than the other way around. The experience left the viewer disoriented and unable to trust the conclusions presented, which the reviewer suspects was the directors' intent.
summary: The film follows disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes in her final weeks before prison as Nathan Fielder moves in with her family. Although the documentary's premise is absurd, the reviewer found the three-hour runtime captivating and worth watching.

content: Scientists have identified a potential link between Earth’s poles that may explain the onset of past ice ages. This process may have disrupted Southern Ocean circulation, enabling the ocean to absorb and store more atmospheric carbon dioxide. The resulting increase in carbon sequestration likely contributed to further planetary cooling.

content:
AI laboratories are increasingly purchasing data from defunct startups to train their models, a trend driven by the limits of public and synthetic datasets. Keelan Miskell, who wound down his crypto startup, sold the company’s codebase and workspace data for tens of thousands of dollars. This growing market involves companies that assist in shutting down startups selling their digital archives to AI labs seeking real-world records to help train AI agents. In a separate feature titled “Are we there yet?”, the newsletter explores the progress of interspecies communication. The article notes that humans are not the only species with communication abilities and that decoding animal communication could reveal the inner lives of other species. Advances in AI and a growing arsenal of devices have made it easier to study animal sounds, such as howls, squeaks, and clicks, although making sense of this data remains complex. The story is part of a series that evaluates six technologies on a progress meter.

The newsletter also highlights a narrated podcast episode discussing the challenges of building a city on the moon. The US and China are racing to build lunar bases, with NASA aiming to establish a small lunar city by the end of the century. The moon’s hostile environment presents significant obstacles, including falling asteroids, cosmic radiation, sharp lunar dust, and extreme temperature swings. A sprawling base would require autonomous robots, nuclear power, and the use of lunar resources for self-sustainability, though political will may be the chief obstacle.

Hackers disrupted the US Federal Election Commission’s website a week before the midterms, hiding spending data during what is described as the costliest midterms ever. Additionally, restrictions on Starlink in Ukraine have driven US allies to rethink their dependence on the service, spooking European officials and providing a pitch for rival services. Greenhouse gas levels, including carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide, are reaching new records worldwide.

Other notable stories include Chinese scientists developing a catalyst to convert Martian atmospheric carbon dioxide into liquid methanol for rocket fuel. Tech billionaires, including Sergey Brin and Eric Schmidt, have funded a major campaign against California’s wealth tax. Delaware is planning to allow AI agents to run entire businesses, a proposal that could let owners evade responsibility for harm. Furthermore, Palmer Luckey has unveiled plans for Anduril to build rugged, American-made military laptops in Ohio using Qualcomm chips.

The newsletter concludes with a quote from Matthew Prince, Cloudflare’s chief executive, who stated that for the next two years, there will be a critical, internet-wide vulnerability every week on average, as AI finds software vulnerabilities faster than they can be patched. A final article examines Apple’s strategy to become net zero by the end of the decade by planting millions of eucalyptus trees in Brazil, a move critics warn may do more harm than good.

title: Antarctic sea ice decline drives rapid salinity shift in Southern Ocean
content:
Scientists report that the rapid decline of Antarctic sea ice since 2016 has triggered a significant shift in Earth’s climate system. In a paper published Wednesday, researchers documented a sharp increase in salinity within Antarctic Intermediate Water, a vast layer of the Southern Ocean located between 2,300 and 4,000 feet deep. This change reverses decades of freshening and mirrors ocean shifts typically associated with major global climate changes over millennia, yet it is occurring within just a few years.

The implications of this salinity increase may extend beyond Antarctica. Bishakhdatta Gayen, a researcher and professor at the University of Melbourne and the Centre for Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences in Bengaluru, India, explained that this water layer spreads northward into the Indian, Pacific, and Atlantic oceans. As it moves, it transports heat, carbon, oxygen, and nutrients toward the tropics and across the equator.
summary: Researchers documented a sharp salinity increase in Antarctic Intermediate Water, reversing decades of freshening since 2016. This layer transports heat, carbon, and nutrients northward into the Indian, Pacific, and Atlantic oceans.

title: AI‑assisted coding fuels surge of bizarre video game mashups on social media
content: AI tools are making it easier to modify and recreate games, raising questions about piracy, copyright and how far the technology could disrupt the industry • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here If your social media algorithms have clocked that you’re into video games, something strange will have happened in the past few weeks. Your feed, like mine, will have been full of clips of streamers playing bizarre mashups of popular video games. Skyrim in Minecraft. Halo, except the main character is Mario. Skate 2 in Call of Duty maps. A flood of professional-looking fan-coded game mods that are mildly interesting to look at for 30 seconds, but ultimately inconsequential. Would I download a mod that lets me play Wii Bowling inside a zombie shooter? No, but I am very interested in where they came from. Of course, the answer – or at least, most of the answer – is AI. After a week of researching this (thanks especially to Replay Mode on YouTube for this informative video, which set me down this track) I now understand that these mashup mods are not just AI-generated videos, but AI-assisted coding. Basically, as of a few weeks ago, Anthropic’s Claude has become extremely good at decompiling video game code. Games are written by humans in readable code and then compiled into binary 1s and 0s that the PC or console running it can read; decompiling is the reversal of that process, revealing a game’s source code, which humans can then edit and mess around with for fun. This used to be an extremely laborious process. But now it is not, because humans aren’t doing much of it any more.
summary: AI‑assisted coding fuels surge of bizarre video game mashups on social media.

Officials reported that at least 64 people were killed after two trains carrying a total of 544 passengers collided, causing several carriages to derail.

title: Black holes can split in two only if spinning at maximum speed
content: Scientists have long known that when two black holes collide, they merge to create a more massive black hole. These events are so violent that they set the very fabric of space ringing with ripples called gravitational waves. Now, new research suggests that the opposite may happen, too: single black holes may be able to split in two. But this can only happen if that progenitor black hole is spinning at maximum possible speed. That speed prevents the black holes from immediately falling back on each other. There are physical laws in place that would usually prevent black holes from splitting in two; the team behind this research investigated whether there are conditions in which these laws can be temporarily bypassed. One of the key aspects of physics that prevents black holes from bifurcating comes from thermodynamics. Black holes possess a characteristic called " entropy," which is essentially a measure of disorder within a system. Imagine a toddler's crayon box. When entropy is low, the crayons are neatly arranged by color. As entropy is increased, the crayons are scattered and no longer in order. To get the crayons back in order, it requires a parent to put energy into the system and neatly reorder the crayons. In other words, the entropy of a system can't be reduced without some intervention and energy being added from outside that system. Parenting would be a little easier if it could. A black hole splitting in two would represent a decrease in entropy, strongly disfavored by the laws of thermodynamics, but only if the black hole is not rotating. The situation could be different for a rapidly rotating black hole. This team of scientists found that a loophole exists for such a black hole. "The two resulting black holes must also be able to separate rather than immediately fall back together," team member Francesco Sannino of the University of Naples Federico II in Italy said in a statement. "When we include this requirement, the window largely closes again, except possibly for black holes rotating close to their maximum possible rate." Black hole trousers? The team calculated just how such a black hole split could occur, finding that the division of the black hole's outer boundary, or "event horizon," proceeds in an oddly trouser-like shape, with one resulting black hole slipping down each "leg." They termed this "pair-of-pants topologies." The researchers also determined that a split is more likely to take place if one of the resultant black holes is considerably smaller than its newly born twin. An illustration of a black hole splitting in two, creating the shape of pants. (Image credit: Francesco Sannino) "We cannot yet give a single probability for a black hole to split. It depends on how gravity behaves beyond Einstein's theory, and we are working to quantify this," Sannino said. "We expect small primordial black holes to be more prone to splitting than much larger astrophysical black holes." Sannino added that such black hole splits may be detectable in high-energy light called gamma-rays. "We may detect a split indirectly: gamma-ray telescopes such as Fermi-LAT can search for signals from tiny black-hole fragments that might form during mergers," the researcher concluded. The team's research was published on Oct. 22 in the journal Physical Review D.
summary: Scientists have long known that when two black holes collide, they merge to create a more massive black hole. These events are so violent that they set the very fabric of space ringing with ripples called gravitational waves.

title: La Bola Negra wins Cannes best director award, eyes Oscars
content: Oozing panache and bagging awards already, La Bola Negra is an eye-popping war and prejudice epic starring Penélope Cruz in a blond wig and Glenn Close speaking Spanish. We meet the ex-lovers who dreamed it up When Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo – the directing duo known in their native Spain as “Los Javis” – began writing their queer epic La Bola Negra, they weren’t thinking about whether it would be stylish (which it is) or win numerous awards (which it has) or capture what they refer to as “the anti-fascist zeitgeist” (which it does). Instead, they thought only of scale. “I’m done with LGBTQ+ movies being niche,” says Ambrossi. “I was like, ‘Let’s make the biggest, gayest war movie ever.’” Job done. At Cannes this year, the best director prize was awarded jointly to them and to Paweł Pawlikowski, who made the Thomas Mann road trip film Fatherland. La Bola Negra is now an Oscars frontrunner, with best picture and best director nominations all but guaranteed. Brimming with panache, the movie darts back and forth between three stories set in Spain: in 1932, a young man applying for membership of an exclusive casino is rejected on the grounds of his suspected homosexuality; in 1937, a callow nationalist soldier develops tender feelings for the injured republican prisoner under his watch; and in 2017, a queer historian inherits an unfinished story by Federico García Lorca. That story lends the movie its title and provides the thread that sews its strands together.
summary: La Bola Negra, a queer war epic directed by Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, received the Cannes best director prize jointly with Paweł Pawlikowski. The film, starring Penélope Cruz and Glenn Close, is now an Oscars frontrunner with best picture and best director nominations all but guaranteed.

title: Ken Russell's 1971 film The Devils restored and rereleased after censorship
content:
Ken Russell’s 1971 film The Devils has been restored and rereleased in its complete form after years of censorship. The film, originally banned for obscenity, is described as a frenzied aria of confrontation and hysteria. It stars Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, who are noted for delivering the performances of their lives in this scabrous classic.

Based on a true story of politically directed mass hysteria, the film was adapted by Russell from Aldous Huxley’s The Devils of Loudun and John Whiting’s stage play The Devils. The narrative centers on Father Urbain Grandier, a 17th-century French priest accused of witchcraft, a role played stylishly by Oliver Reed. In the film, Grandier declares, “I could never be Satan’s boy. I haven’t the humility.”

The review argues that while the film is obscene, the obscenity does not reside in the sexualized images of a crucified Christ or naked nuns. Instead, the text states that the violence of authority is what is shown to be obscene. Russell’s work is presented as a confrontational assault on good taste, depicting what punishments like burning at the stake might actually look like.

The film is situated in an era when movies in high-street cinemas retained the power to shock the polite cultural mainstream. This shock compelled serious discussion regarding whether the resulting ban or the film’s content was justified. The review highlights that the film underscores the violence of power through its intense depiction of these historical events.
summary: The film, based on a true story of mass hysteria and adapted from works by Aldous Huxley and John Whiting, features performances by Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave. It was originally banned for obscenity but is now restored and rereleased in its complete form.

summary: The long‑standing theory that comets delivered the molecular building blocks for life on Earth is challenged by a new study. Comets are known to carry many of these molecules.
author: Phys.org

title: Cyclone eases after lashing India's southeastern coast, no deaths reported
content: A cyclone struck India's southeastern coast on Wednesday, bringing ferocious winds and torrential rain. Officials reported no initial deaths from the storm, which subsequently began to ease after making landfall.
summary: Ferocious winds and torrential rain battered India's southeastern coast after a cyclone made landfall on Wednesday. Officials reported no initial deaths and said the storm later eased.
author: Phys.org

title: Trump Announces Rollback of Methane Emission Rules for Oil and Gas Producers
content: U.S. President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday a significant rollback of regulations designed to limit methane emissions from oil and gas producers. The move targets rules intended to curb the release of methane, identified in the announcement as a greenhouse gas superpollutant.
summary: President Donald Trump announced a sweeping rollback of rules that stop oil and gas producers from emitting methane. The rollback removes restrictions that previously limited methane emissions from these producers.
author: Phys.org

title: Finnish goddess Kivutar stores pain in a mountain and heals by transforming it
content: In Finnish lore, the goddess Kivutar stashes away pain in a mountain for safekeeping. She also serves as a healer, channeling that pain into rocks or boiling it down into a less potent form in a huge vat.
summary: In Finnish lore, the goddess Kivutar stashes pain in a mountain for safekeeping. She also heals by channeling the pain into rocks or boiling it into a less potent form in a huge vat.
author: Phys.org

title: Oxford Chemists Map Polymer-to-Hard Carbon Transformation with Machine Learning
content: A new study published in Chemical Science shows researchers from the University of Oxford’s Department of Chemistry used machine‑learning simulations to trace how a common polymer transforms into hard carbon. The simulations reveal the atomic‑scale processes that give this technologically important material its disordered structure.
summary: Researchers from the University of Oxford's Department of Chemistry published a study in Chemical Science that used machine learning simulations to trace how a common polymer transforms into hard carbon. The simulations reveal the atomic-scale processes that give hard carbon its disordered structure.
author: Phys.org

title: Dead Tree Branches Move Daily as Humidity Changes, Laser Scans Show
content: Geoinformatics researchers at Heidelberg University, in cooperation with the Finnish Geospatial Research Institute (FGI), have revealed that dead tree branches are not static but move throughout the day. Their study, which utilized laser scans, demonstrated that these branches rise and fall in response to changing humidity levels.
summary: Dead tree branches move throughout the day, not staying static. Geoinformatics researchers at Heidelberg University, working with the Finnish Geospatial Research Institute, tracked these movements in a study.
author: Phys.org

title: Aerogel start-ups aim to insulate millions of historic UK and European homes
content: Millions of old homes across the UK and Europe require insulation to meet net‑zero strategies. Promising start‑ups say that aerogels—a super‑insulating solid—could provide the needed solution.
summary: Millions of old homes across the UK and Europe need insulating under net-zero strategies. Promising start-ups believe aerogel materials could be the answer.
author: New Scientist

title: Experts assess TikTok's “ferritin face” claims linking skin changes to iron deficiency
content: TikTok influencers have popularised the term “ferritin face” to describe a set of features—pallor, dark circles under the eyes, dry skin and hair loss—that they claim signal low iron stores. Health experts note that while symptoms such as dark circles, grey‑toned skin, cracked lips and hair loss can indeed be warning signs of iron deficiency, they can also arise from a range of other causes. The discussion centres on whether the social‑media narrative reflects medical fact and when individuals should consult a GP for assessment.
summary: Experts assess TikTok's “ferritin face” claims linking skin changes to iron deficiency.
author: Guardian Science

title: Video outlines perimenopause symptoms, tests and treatment misinformation
content: A new video on perimenopause notes that the topic has become widely discussed, with celebrities sharing personal experiences and doctors posting advice online. The program highlights that, alongside growing awareness, a rising number of women are encountering misinformation about treatments such as hormone‑replacement therapy (HRT). In the segment, Madeleine Finlay speaks with Dr Paula Briggs, a consultant in sexual and reproductive health, about why experts have raised an alarm. Science correspondent Nicola Davis then outlines the facts on perimenopause symptoms, testing and treatment options.
summary: Perimenopause is a hot topic with celebrities sharing experiences and doctors offering advice online. In the video, Madeleine Finlay talks to Dr Paula Briggs, a consultant in sexual and reproductive health, while Nicola Davis presents facts on symptoms, tests and treatments amid HRT misinformation.
author: Guardian Science

title: Scientists map 10,000-year sea‑level rise that turned inland hills into Venice lagoon
content:
Scientists have identified ancient hills and swamps that vanished as sea levels rose across the northern Adriatic. Their findings indicate that the ground beneath Venice, now famed as a floating city, once lay many miles inland.  

Research led by Samuele Ongaro of the University of Southampton and collaborators used seismic data and sedimentary cores from coastal basins in northern Italy, Slovenia and northern Croatia. The team modeled sea‑level changes and reconstructed the region’s landscape over the past 10,000 years, showing how rising waters reshaped the coastline and submerged former land.
summary: Scientists map 10,000-year sea‑level rise that turned inland hills into Venice lagoon.
author: Guardian Science

title: NASA Curiosity rover prepares to drill at Nazca site on Mars
content: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 4 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5043-5049: Preparing to Drill at ‘Nazca’ NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this close-up image using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), showing the abundance of roughly disc-shaped potential crystal forms on our next drill target, informally named “Nazca.” The scratches made by the DRT brush are also visible in this image. MAHLI, located on the turret at the end of the rover’s robotic arm, uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different focus positions, to bring multiple features into focus in a single image. Curiosity composed the image on Oct. 18, 2026, Sol 5048 (Martian day 5,048 of the Mars Science Laboratory Mission), at 12:19:51 UTC. NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS Written by Lucy Lim, Planetary Scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 16, 2026 Following the Basque Lakes drill campaign, Curiosity has returned to a spot just a few meters away from the “Chiu Chiu” block to conduct our next drill campaign. “Chiu Chiu” itself wasn’t a good candidate for drilling but the block just beyond it was much more promising, so it became our drive target during Monday’s planning. I was on planning Friday as Geology and Mineralogy Science Theme Lead when we received our close-up views of the neighbor block from the post-drive imaging and our team was happy to see that it was jam-packed with the “disc- and needle-” shaped lumps, just like “Chiu Chiu.” We quickly gave the science go-ahead to proceed with preparations for drilling at the newly named “Nazca” site. One major hypothesis about how the “discs and needles” texture formed is that the characteristic shapes were originally created during the growth of crystals, or “crystal forms.” Minerals will tend to grow into specific shapes depending on their microscopic crystal structure, similar to the salt crystals that you can grow in your kitchen as a home science project. (Maybe you have grown one of those for a science class in school!) The relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at “Nazca” and “Chiu Chiu” are providing clues about the temperature at the time when they grew and the availability of salts and fluids. However, we can’t necessarily assume that the modern-day composition represents the original mineral because sometimes mineral crystals are replaced by other minerals some time after original crystallization. The new minerals are then known as “pseudomorphs” because they have the same shape as the first minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure. As we prepared for the drill preload test, we also planned several special observations aimed at highly detailed characterization of the crystal forms. MAHLI will execute a Quantitative Relief Model (“QRM”) observation consisting of five overlapping images at slightly different geometries. The combination of these will enable a detailed three-dimensional relief model to be constructed. In addition, MAHLI will also add extra frames to its highest-resolution imaging by doubling the number of focus mechanism steps. Together, these observations will increase the resolution of the 3D models we will have of the crystal forms. Meanwhile, the ChemCam LIBS will conduct a “depth profile” experiment to obtain compositional information from slightly deeper layers within a nearby crystal-form-rich target, “Toucan”. Normally the 150 LIBS laser shots from each sol’s observation are spaced out over a five-point raster at 30 shots per point, but this time we are concentrating all 150 laser shots on the same spot on the rock. Since each laser shot vaporizes a very small amount of the rock to form a plasma, the 150-shot profile should penetrate approximately five times deeper than a normal 30-shot point observation. We will thus be able to observe the composition deeper inside the exposed crystal form and see whether it’s different from the surface-level composition. There are several reasons this could be the case including exposure of the surface to the modern Martian environment and also the circumstances in which the crystal form developed originally, so it’s an experiment worth pursuing. The LIBS, DRT and APXS will also be applied to the “Nazca” spot before the preload test to characterize its surface composition as thoroughly as possible before drilling. The third LIBS of the plan will go to “Condor,” a nearby block in which a finely layered texture is exposed. We also continued to observe the modern Martian environment as twilight cloud season begins. In this plan we included some nighttime imaging of the larger and brighter of Mars’ two satellites, Phobos. Capturing images of Phobos and the nearby sky when Phobos is full can show sunlight reflecting off the moon and scattering in the Martian atmosphere, providing a good way to estimate the particle sizes in the Martian clouds. We can do similar measurements sometimes with solar observations, but the Phobos data allow us to measure cloud particle sizes later in the night. We expect to be measuring high-altitude carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) clouds in this observation. Want to read more posts from the Curiosity team? title: ICE's HSI runs one of the largest anti‑left surveillance operations in US
content: ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations is conducting extensive surveillance of left‑wing activists, a program described as rivaling the FBI and CIA’s historic crackdowns on the civil‑rights and anti‑war movements. The operation is characterized as one of the largest anti‑left surveillance efforts in U.S. history.
summary: ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations is conducting far‑reaching spying against left‑wing activists. The operation is described as rivaling FBI and CIA crackdowns on the Civil Rights and anti‑war movements.
author: Wired

title: Men spend $50,000 to reserve a Tesla Roadster as base model costs far more
content: The base model—without thrusters or the flight system—will likely cost several times that amount to buy. “I’m going to do everything in my power to get the flying one,” says one customer.
summary: Some men are paying $50,000 to reserve a Tesla Roadster. The base model without thrusters or a flight system would likely cost several times that amount, and one customer said he will do everything to get the flying version.

title: Portland Fermentation Festival held last week as sauerkraut, kimchi gain spotlight
content: The annual Portland Fermentation Festival took place last week in Oregon, at a time when sauerkraut, kimchi, and other funky foods are in the social and political spotlight.
summary: The annual Portland Fermentation Festival was held last week in Oregon. Sauerkraut, kimchi and other fermented foods are currently in the social and political spotlight.
author: Wired

title: Meta launches “Waddle World” AI pet journal app
content:
Meta has quietly launched a new app called Waddle World. The app is described as a “tamagotchi‑style” pet game in which virtual creatures chat with users and create doodles to illustrate those conversations.

According to its Apple and Play Store listings, the 16‑bit pet care game is actually “a daily journal disguised as a pet.” Users are encouraged to talk, not type, to their pixel pets, and can also play “cozy games” such as stacking groceries or word games. The Play Store description calls the experience “a little friend that listens” and a cozy world where a hatchable virtual pet lives, inviting users to visit whenever they like.
summary: Meta has launched a tamagotchi‑style pet game called Waddle World that is described as a daily journal disguised as a pet. The virtual pets chat with users, create doodles and offer cozy activities such as stacking groceries or word games.
author: The Verge

title: Meta considered whisper strategy to turn academics against Jonathan Haidt
content:
Meta was feeling public pressure over teen mental health and facing an impending onslaught of kids safety trials, the company considered a campaign to discredit a key critic: social psychologist Jonathan Haidt.  

Newly filed court documents show that in March 2023, Meta discussed a “Whisper strategy” to “turn academics against Haidt,” a thought leader who blamed social media for rising adolescent depression and anxiety.  

Haidt hadn’t yet published his bestselling book, The Anxious Generation, but he testified about his conclusions before Congress in 2022, and in February 2023, he began posting more of his theories and research to Substack.
summary: Meta considered a "whisper strategy" to turn academics against social psychologist Jonathan Haidt in March 2023, according to newly filed court documents. Haidt had testified before Congress in 2022 about social media's role in adolescent depression and anxiety, and began publishing his theories on Substack in February 2023.
author: The Verge

title: South Africa tests 7.6-kilometre freight train in bid to break world record
content: South Africa’s state‑owned logistics firm Transnet reported that it tested a freight train measuring 7.6 kilometres in length, composed of 696 empty wagons. The train was run over an 860‑kilometre route from Saldanha Bay to an inland iron‑ore mine, a trial Transnet described as the world’s longest freight train.
summary: Transnet tested the world's longest freight train, measuring 7.6 kilometres and consisting of 696 empty wagons. The train travelled 860 kilometres from Saldanha Bay to an inland iron ore mine.
author: Euronews

title: Israel election deadlock; Finland and Norway leaders call Putin
content:
Israel’s recent election has ended in a clear deadlock, with neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot positioned to secure a majority.  

In Europe, Finland’s and Norway’s leaders have called Vladimir Putin as the continent seeks a seat at the table. The coverage also notes Serbia’s vote, the upcoming U.S. mid‑terms, and Mbappé’s dispute with China.
summary: Israel's election ended in apparent deadlock with neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot on track for a majority. Leaders of Finland and Norway have phoned Vladimir Putin as Europe seeks a seat at the table.
author: Euronews

title: Russian drone strike in Kharkiv injures five, sparks building fires
content:
A Russian drone strike on Kharkiv injured five people, including a 4‑year‑old child.  

The attack set several buildings ablaze, and firefighters were working under the threat of further strikes.
summary: A Russian drone strike on Kharkiv overnight injured five people, including a 4-year-old child. The attack set several buildings on fire, and firefighters are battling the blazes amid the threat of additional strikes.
author: Euronews

title: Brazil's President Lula celebrates 81st birthday after re‑election win
content: Brazil’s re‑elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva marked his 81st birthday on Tuesday, 27 October, surrounded by dozens of supporters outside the Alvorada presidential palace in Brasília. The celebration came just two days after he won a closely contested election.
summary: Brazil's re‑elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated his 81st birthday on Tuesday, 27 October. He was joined by dozens of supporters outside the Alvorada presidential palace in Brasília, two days after his closely contested election victory.
author: Euronews

title: First aerial images show aftermath of high‑speed train collision near Urda, Toledo
content: Aerial footage has been released showing the aftermath of a collision between two high‑speed trains near Urda in Spain’s Toledo province. Emergency crews are continuing rescue and response operations at the site of the deadly train crash.
summary: Aerial footage shows the aftermath of a collision between two high‑speed trains near Urda in Spain’s Toledo province. Emergency crews continue rescue and response operations at the site.
author: Euronews

title: Spain train crash near Toledo leaves at least 10 dead, wreckage footage released
content: First footage of the crash near Toledo shows the wreckage of two derailed high‑speed train carriages. At least 10 people have died, rescuers are searching the debris, and authorities have warned the death toll could rise.
summary: At least 10 people died when a high-speed train struck another near Toledo, Spain. Two carriages derailed and rescuers were searching through the wreckage as authorities warned the death toll could rise.
author: Euronews

title: At least 10 killed in high‑speed train crash in Toledo, Spain
content: At least ten people were killed when two trains collided in central Spain on Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo. Following the crash, rail service has been suspended on the route linking Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia, according to France 24 correspondent Sarah Morris.
summary: At least ten people died in a crash between two high‑speed trains in central Spain on Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo. Rail service has been suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia.
author: France 24

title: Israelis await election results as Arab-led parties make historic showing
content: Israelis are waiting for the final election results, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu still far from being defeated. Arab‑led parties have achieved a historic showing, though it remains uncertain whether other anti‑Netanyahu factions will join them to form a parliamentary majority. The sensitivity of issues concerning Palestinians and their descendants continues to shape the political landscape, and France 24 international affairs commentator Douglas Herbert offers further analysis.
summary: Arab-led parties appear to have made a historic showing in the Israeli election. Commentator Douglas Herbert says it is unclear whether other opponents of Netanyahu's government will join them to form a majority coalition, as issues involving Palestinians remain highly sensitive.
author: France 24

title: Flavio Bolsonaro heading to Ecuador from Argentina after fleeing Brazil
content: Argentina’s government said on Wednesday, Oct. 28, that defeated right‑wing presidential candidate and 45‑year‑old senator Flavio Bolsonaro was traveling to Ecuador after fleeing Brazil. The Trump administration had granted Bolsonaro and his family U.S. visas the previous day, a development reported by France 24’s Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson.
summary: Defeated right‑wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro was on his way to Ecuador after fleeing Brazil, Argentina’s government said on Wednesday, October 28. The 45‑year‑old senator and his family had been granted United States visas the day before by the Trump administration.
author: France 24

title: Israeli election: papers label hope for pro- and anti‑Netanyahu parties as wishful thinking
content: On Wednesday, October 28, a press review noted that newspapers are reacting to the ongoing election results in Israel. The same review also previewed stories about Macklemore’s upcoming Free Palestine tour in Paris, new findings on antidepressants, and a look at boomer divorcées’ dating lives.
summary: Israeli newspapers comment on the ongoing election results in Israel. The coverage describes expectations for both pro‑Netanyahu and anti‑Netanyahu parties as wishful thinking.
author: France 24

title: At least 10 killed as two trains collide on Madrid-Seville route in southern Spain
content:
Two trains traveling in opposite directions collided on the Madrid‑Seville line in southern Spain. Local authorities have confirmed at least ten fatalities, while some media outlets have reported a possible toll of up to thirty‑nine deaths. The cause of the collision has not been determined.

The incident has revived memories of a deadly train crash in Córdoba earlier this year. France 24 correspondent Sarah Morris is reporting live from Madrid with further updates.
summary: Two trains traveling in opposite directions collided on the Madrid‑Seville route in southern Spain. Local authorities have confirmed at least 10 deaths, while some media reports suggest the toll could be as high as 39.
author: France 24

title: Netanyahu nears 61-seat threshold as Israeli election results await
content:
Israel’s election results are still pending, with final tallies expected tonight or tomorrow morning. Current indications suggest a growing advantage for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his bloc, though he remains short of the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority.

Netanyahu addressed his supporters at the National Congress Centre at approximately 3 a.m. local time. France 24’s correspondent Clovis Casali reported live from Jerusalem with the latest updates.
summary: The final results are expected tonight or tomorrow morning. For now, the picture is looking increasingly favourable for Benjamin Netanyahu and his bloc, but the Israeli prime minister is still short of a clear victory, as he needs 61 seats to secure a parliamentary majority.
author: France 24

title: Arizona food stamp cuts spark voter anger ahead of US midterms
content: With the U.S. midterm elections less than a week away, cost of living has become a central campaign issue. In Arizona, many Americans are criticizing the administration’s decision to slash food stamps, a move they say has had significant consequences for the poorest. The report is by Camille Corcoran.
summary: The administration's decision to slash food stamps in Arizona has angered many voters. The cost of living has emerged as a key campaign issue as the US midterm elections approach within a week.
author: France 24

title: Ceasefire in Russian‑occupied Oleshky holds for first 30 hours
content: A ceasefire that began on Tuesday in Oleshky, a Russian‑occupied city in southern Ukraine, held through its first day and night, despite ongoing fighting between Moscow and Kyiv elsewhere. The truce is expected to remain in place until Sunday, reports Emerald Maxwell.
summary: A local ceasefire in the Russian‑occupied southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky held through its first day and night. The truce, which began on Tuesday, is expected to remain in place until Sunday.
author: France 24

title: Serbian police kill minor who attacked guard at Israeli embassy in Belgrade
content: Serbian police shot dead a minor who attacked a guard at Israel’s embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister said. Interior Minister Ivica Dacic added that police declared the highest terror alert after the incident.
summary: Police in Serbia shot dead a minor who attacked a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives. Interior minister Ivica Dacic said the highest terror alert was declared after the incident.
author: DW World

title: Russia vows historic return to Africa after Ukraine invasion
content: Russia, after its invasion of Ukraine and the ensuing rift with Western nations, announced that it intends to make a “historic return” to Africa. The statement signals Moscow’s plan to re‑engage the continent following the conflict‑driven diplomatic split.
summary: Russia says it will make a historic return to Africa after its invasion of Ukraine created a rift with the West. The content does not detail any specific actions taken so far.
author: DW World

title: EU's 'Made in Europe' auto push worries suppliers from Turkey, Morocco, Japan
content: EU’s “Made in Europe” initiative, aimed at shielding European carmakers from Chinese competition, is raising concerns among global auto suppliers. The policy could negatively affect partners from Turkey and Morocco, as well as from Japan and South Korea, with billions of euros in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs at stake.
summary: The EU's effort to shield Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals could harm close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.
author: DW World

title: Ireland marks 300th anniversary of Jonathan Swift’s Gulliver’s Travels
content:
Events across Ireland are marking the 300th anniversary of Jonathan Swift’s classic satire, Gulliver’s Travels. In March 1726, Swift, then the dean of St Patrick’s Cathedral in Dublin, traveled to London and had a courier deliver his manuscript to a publisher under cover of night. Anticipating that the novel would cause trouble, the Irish clergyman sought to publish it anonymously.

The satirical work, originally titled Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World, was released in October 1726 and became an instant hit. Three centuries later, the book is widely recognized as Gulliver’s Travels, prompting current celebrations of its origins and cultural impact.
summary: Events in Ireland are exploring the origins of Jonathan Swift’s novel, published anonymously in October 1726 as Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World. The satirical work, better known today as Gulliver’s Travels, is being celebrated three centuries after its first publication.
author: Guardian World

title: Spain train crash kills at least 30 in Toledo province
content:
At least 30 people were killed when two high‑speed trains collided in Toledo province, central Spain, on the line between Madrid and Seville. The collision reportedly involved a high‑speed service running into the back of another train, knocking two carriages off the track.

Footage broadcast by the regional channel CMM TV showed a derailed train with at least one carriage still on an elevated section of track. The scene also displayed twisted metal, broken panels and wreckage scattered across an embankment beneath the line.
summary: At least 30 people were killed when two high‑speed trains collided on the Madrid‑Seville line in Toledo province, central Spain. CMM TV footage showed a derailed train with a carriage on an elevated track and wreckage strewn across an embankment.
author: Guardian World

title: At least 30 dead after two high‑speed trains collide in Toledo, Spain
content: Spain’s rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo Full report from Spain At least 30 people are believed to have died after two high-speed trains collided in the province of Toledo in Spain, with concerns the death toll could be much higher. The number of people affected is expected to rise ( 10:46 ), local authorities said, with growing concerns about a “major tragedy” ( 11:03 ). The affected trains are understood to be Iryo 7076 with 146 passengers plus one baby on board, and AVE 2080 with 397 passengers on board, making it 544 people in total on board of both train ( 11:00 ). The incident comes less than a year after a similar crash in Adamuz, the province of Córdoba, which killed 46 and injured 152 in January this year ( 11:00 ). Spain’s high-speed railway network ranks as the largest in Europe and the second biggest in the world after China, carrying 25 million passengers in 2024. Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sánchez said he was “shocked” by the accident ( 11:05 ), with transport minister Óscar Puente working at the emergency control centre to “obtain all possible information about what happened” ( 11:16 ). Updated at 10:50am UK to reflect the new death toll “In the [emergency] control center since 9:40 trying to obtain all possible information about what happened.”
summary: At least 30 dead after two high‑speed trains collide in Toledo, Spain.
author: Guardian World

content: As next week’s all but certain rate rise looms, there is one thing we can all agree on: the end of war in the Middle East can’t come soon enough Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast Jim Chalmers is blaming the latest shocking inflation figures on the worsening Middle East conflict, and he has a point. title: Alastair Campbell urges Australia to re‑win democratic politics after Haines attack
content: Tony Blair’s former spokesperson says attacks on UK MPs did not bring about lasting cultural change and overheated rhetoric quickly returned to politics Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Tony Blair’s former communications guru, Alastair Campbell, says the UK political system was too quick to revert to overheated rhetoric and polarisation after attacks on MPs, urging politicians to “re-win the argument for democratic politics”. summary: Tony Blair’s former communications guru Alastair Campbell said the UK political system quickly reverted to overheated rhetoric after attacks on MPs. He urged Australian politicians to “re‑win the argument for democratic politics” after independent MP Helen Haines was allegedly targeted in an attack outside her northern Victoria electorate office that left her without both legs.
