title: Mexican police retract claim they found missing Arizona woman Shayna Feinman alive
content: Mexican police had said they found Shayna Feinman in Tijuana, raising the hopes of missing Arizonan’s family Arizona authorities say their Mexican counterparts were resoundingly mistaken when they publicly claimed recently that they found alive a woman who was feared slain after disappearing in 2024 – a turn of events that her sister has called “turmoil” and “heartbreaking”. The case in question centers on Shayna Feinman, who was reported missing in rural Yavapai county, Arizona, in March 2024 at age 38.
summary: Mexican police said they had found Shayna Feinman alive in Tijuana, raising hopes for her family. Arizona authorities later said the claim was mistaken, and her sister called the situation turmoil and heartbreaking.
author: Guardian World

title: Africa CDC chief warns unprecedented Ebola outbreak could reach UK
content:
Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), has warned that the current Ebola outbreak could spread across borders like the Covid pandemic unless additional funding is secured for preparedness and treatment.  

The outbreak has already reached 10,000 cases, with almost 5,000 deaths reported. Kaseya described the spread as “unprecedented” and cautioned that it could reach the United Kingdom and other countries.  

He compared the situation to the Covid pandemic, noting that Covid first took hold in China before spreading worldwide, claiming millions of lives and severely damaging health systems and economies.
summary: Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, said the unprecedented Ebola outbreak could reach the UK and other countries. He noted the outbreak has reached 10,000 cases and almost 5,000 deaths and warned more funding is needed for preparedness and possible treatment.
author: Guardian World

title: Cricket Australia takes $20m revenue hit from two-day Ashes Tests with more losses ahead
content:
Cricket Australia reported a $20 million revenue loss from the pair of two‑day Ashes Tests held last summer. The hit is expected to weaken the sport’s bottom line as the governing body prepares for several years of financial deficits.

Despite the blow, the organization announced an $82 million surplus for the 2025‑26 season, driven by strong broadcast interest, ticket sales and commercial revenue linked to the men’s Ashes. Cricket Australia also projects two years of deficits and notes reduced interest in upcoming tours.
summary: Cricket Australia reported an $82m surplus for the 2025-26 season. The organization also said a $20m revenue hit from last summer's two-day Ashes Tests will lead to deficits in the coming years.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Kurtley Beale recalled to Wallabies squad for UK spring tour
content:
Veteran playmaker Kurtley Beale has been recalled to the Wallabies squad for the upcoming spring tour of the United Kingdom. The 37‑year‑old, who could add to a career total of 95 caps, answered a call from coach Les Kiss on Wednesday and will join the squad for the three Tests against England, Scotland and Wales next month.

The recall comes ahead of the inaugural Nations Championship finals in the UK, scheduled for 21‑23 November. Alongside Beale, James Ramm and Kalani Thomas are also set to travel with the team as Australia prepares for the 2027 Rugby World Cup hosted in Australia.
summary: Kurtley Beale recalled to Wallabies squad for UK spring tour.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Bayern Munich stay unbeaten, beat Freiburg, tribute to Kompany
content: Bayern Munich secured a victory over Freiburg, allowing the German champions to reclaim the top spot in the Bundesliga standings. The win came amid the absence of manager Vincent Kompany, who is currently hospitalized after collapsing while observing Bayern’s second‑team training session. The club paid tribute to Kompany during the match.
summary: Bayern Munich beat Freiburg to return to the top of the Bundesliga. The club paid tribute to manager Vincent Kompany, who is recovering in hospital after collapsing while watching the second team train.
author: BBC Sport

title: Unattached former Everton defender Seamus Coleman says he is contemplating retirement
content: Seamus Coleman, the former Everton defender who is currently unattached, says he is contemplating retirement from football. However, he added that he does not want to “completely draw a line in the sand” on his playing career.
summary: Former Everton defender Seamus Coleman says he is contemplating retiring from football. He said he does not want to completely draw a line in the sand on his career.
author: BBC Sport

title: Dowman sees red as Arsenal dumped out by Fleetwood Town in Carabao Cup
content: Arsenal was eliminated from the Carabao Cup last-16 by League Two side Fleetwood Town in a match described as dramatic and shocking. The article notes that the defeat involved a red card, a penalty shootout, and a drone, while questioning whether Mikel Arteta went too far in the incident.
summary: Arsenal lost to League Two Fleetwood Town in the last-16 of the Carabao Cup. The match featured a red card, a penalty shootout, and a drone.
author: BBC Sport

title: Fleetwood beat Arsenal in Carabao Cup penalty shootout
content: Fleetwood Town advanced to the Carabao Cup quarter-finals by defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout. The match concluded with an 83-place gap between the two teams in the league standings.
summary: Fleetwood advanced to the Carabao Cup quarter-final by defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout. The two teams were separated by 83 league places before the match.
author: BBC Sport

title: Obama's Cheesecake Factory jab sparks GOP‑Democrat midterm spat
content: A comment by former President Obama regarding The Cheesecake Factory has escalated into a political dispute between the GOP and Democrats. The Hill reports that this exchange has intensified as the competitive midterm election cycle approaches its conclusion.
summary: Former President Obama made a Cheesecake Factory jab. The comment sparked a spat between the GOP and Democrats as the midterm election cycle nears its end.
author: The Hill

title: 4 Democratic senators urge Trump to restore canceled green funds for permitting bill
content: A group of four Democratic senators sent a letter to the bipartisan negotiators of a permitting reform bill, expressing distrust that the Trump administration will treat renewable energy fairly under the legislation. The senators are calling on the administration to restore climate funding that was terminated for blue states, arguing that this action is necessary to earn trust for the proposed permit reform bill.
summary: Four Democratic senators have expressed distrust that the Trump administration will treat renewable energy fairly under a bipartisan permitting reform bill. They are urging the administration to restore climate funding that was terminated for blue states.
author: The Hill

title: Trump Announces Plan to Loosen Methane Rules at Lubbock Rally
content: President Trump announced plans to loosen methane regulations for the oil and gas sector during a rally in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday night. This was his second campaign stop of the day in the state, where he aimed to support the Senate campaign of Republican Ken Paxton, the state attorney general.
summary: President Trump announced plans to loosen methane regulations for the oil and gas sector during a rally in Lubbock, Texas. The announcement was made during his second campaign stop of the day, where he also sought to aid Republican Ken Paxton's Senate campaign.
author: The Hill

title: Mike Johnson Promises Peaceful Transfer of Power on Jan 3
content: House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) announced on Tuesday that a “peaceful transfer of power” will occur when new members join the House next year. While affirming the peaceful nature of the transition, Johnson stated that the current majority will be retained.
summary: House Speaker Mike Johnson said there will be a peaceful transfer of power on Jan 3 when new House members join next year. He added that the transfer will not happen because they will keep the majority.
author: The Hill

title: Sen. Lisa Murkowski Endorses Democrat Jonathan Kreiss‑Tomkins for Alaska Governor
content: Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) endorsed Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins for governor on Tuesday, choosing the former state lawmaker over three Republican candidates. In a statement released by Kreiss-Tomkins’ campaign, Murkowski praised his commitment to bipartisanship, arguing that Alaska needs a governor willing to work with lawmakers from both parties.
summary: Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) endorsed Democrat Jonathan Kreiss‑Tomkins in Alaska’s governor’s race. She praised him for his commitment to bipartisanship, saying Alaska needs a governor willing to work with lawmakers from both parties.
author: The Hill

title: Federal grand jury declines to indict Cassidy Hutchinson over Jan. 6 testimony
content: A federal grand jury in Washington, D.C., rejected the Justice Department’s attempt to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson on Tuesday. The decision concerns her testimony to lawmakers regarding President Trump’s actions during the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol. Justice Department attorney Neville Hedley informed U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui of the grand jury’s action.
summary: A federal grand jury in Washington, D. C., on Tuesday rejected the Justice Department’s attempt to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson over her testimony to lawmakers about President Trump’s actions during the Jan.
author: The Hill

title: Trump jokes Ted Cruz would be his pick for Supreme Court vacancy
content:
President Trump joked on Tuesday that Senator Ted Cruz (R‑Texas) would be his pick for the next Supreme Court vacancy, adding that Cruz could receive unanimous confirmation because lawmakers from both parties would eagerly support his appointment to replace a sitting justice.  
During a mid‑term rally in Lubbock, Texas, Trump praised Cruz, underscoring the senator’s standing in the Republican Party.
summary: President Trump joked on Tuesday that Sen. Ted Cruz would be his pick for the next Supreme Court vacancy, claiming Cruz could be unanimously confirmed because lawmakers from both parties would jump at the chance to get rid of him in Congress. He made the remark during a midterm rally in Lubbock, Texas.
author: The Hill

title: Trump and Talarico Hold Dueling Texas Rallies Ahead of Midterms
content: President Trump and Texas Senate candidate James Talarico (D) held dueling rallies in Texas on Tuesday, one week before the midterm elections. Trump conducted two rallies, in Corpus Christi and Lubbock, marking his fourth trip to the state to support the campaign.
summary: Trump and Talarico Hold Dueling Texas Rallies Ahead of Midterms.
author: The Hill

title: Plan for multibillion-pound Sizewell nuclear plant a ‘terrible deal’ for UK taxpayers, MPs say
content:
The public accounts committee (PAC) has warned that the government's plan to fund a multibillion‑pound nuclear plant at the Sizewell site in Suffolk poses an “extraordinary” risk to bill payers. The committee described the proposal as a “terrible deal” for the UK taxpayer over the rest of the century.

MPs on the PAC said the cost of the Sizewell C nuclear reactor could rise to almost £48 billion. They warned that bill payers would need to provide an additional £9.8 billion to construct the plant before 2040 and an extra £12 billion over its 60‑year operating life.
summary: Plan for multibillion-pound Sizewell nuclear plant a ‘terrible deal’ for UK taxpayers, MPs say.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Trump announces termination of Biden-era methane regulations
content: Critics warn of climate danger as president in Texas claims change will save companies and consumers billions Donald Trump announced his administration is “terminating” Biden-era regulations holding oil and gas companies accountable for large leaks of planet-warming methane during a rally in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday evening. Trump said during a campaign rally in Texas that the change would save consumers and energy producers $45bn and unlock 210 million barrels of oil – equivalent to about 10 days of US petroleum consumption. “Tonight, I’m officially terminating Biden’s expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers,” Trump said, lifting what he called “crippling regulations on methane that caused prices to skyrocket” for small oil and gas operators.
summary: Trump announces termination of Biden-era methane regulations.
author: Guardian Environment

title: ASTRO Updates Prostate Cancer Radiation Therapy Guidelines to Shorter Courses
content:
The American Society for Radiation Oncology (ASTRO) has released an updated clinical guideline on hypofractionated radiation therapy for localized prostate cancer, published in Practical Radiation Oncology. This document supersedes ASTRO’s 2018 recommendations and offers evidence-based guidance for patients undergoing definitive external beam radiation therapy (EBRT).

The new guideline reflects a matured evidence base demonstrating that shorter-course radiation therapy can maintain cancer control while reducing the overall treatment burden for patients.
summary: The American Society for Radiation Oncology (ASTRO) released an updated guideline recommending hypofractionated radiation therapy for localized prostate cancer. The new guideline replaces the 2018 recommendations and was published in Practical Radiation Oncology.
author: Medical Xpress

title: 3D-Printed Implant Prototype Records Brain Activity and Provides Targeted Cooling
content: Researchers from the Leibniz Institute of Polymer Research Dresden (IPF) and the Else Kröner Fresenius Center (EKFZ) for Digital Health at TU Dresden have created a 3D‑printed implant prototype that simultaneously records brain activity and delivers targeted cooling. The prototype was described in a study published in the journal Advanced Science. The authors suggest that this dual‑function device could open new avenues for treating drug‑resistant focal epilepsy.
summary: Researchers from the Leibniz Institute of Polymer Research Dresden (IPF) and the Else Kröner Fresenius Center (EKFZ) for Digital Health at TU Dresden created a 3D-printed implant prototype that records brain activity and provides targeted cooling. The prototype could lead to new treatments for drug-resistant focal epilepsy and was published in Advanced Science.
author: Medical Xpress

title: VCU study finds sphingosine kinase 2 inhibitors may curb obesity and cancer risk
content:
Obesity remains a widespread public health issue in the United States, affecting more than 40 % of adults between August 2021 and 2023. The condition is linked to numerous complications, including an increased risk of cancer.

A study published in Science Advances and led by researchers at the VCU Massey Comprehensive Cancer Center proposes a novel approach to address this problem. The investigators found that selectively inhibiting the enzyme sphingosine kinase 2 in fat cells could reduce obesity and lower the risk of obesity‑related comorbidities such as cancer.
summary: Research published in Science Advances by scientists at VCU Massey Comprehensive Cancer Center found that inhibiting the enzyme sphingosine kinase 2 in fat cells could be a new strategy to combat obesity. The study suggests this approach may also lower the risk of obesity‑related comorbidities such as cancer.
author: Medical Xpress

title: National study finds drop in drug heart infection hospitalizations, stimulant share rises
content: A recent national study reports a decline in hospitalizations for serious heart infections linked to drug use, after years of rising rates. The reduction is largely attributed to fewer cases involving opioids. The findings suggest a shift in the underlying drug‑related causes of these infections.
summary: National study finds drop in drug heart infection hospitalizations, stimulant share rises.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Neural network improves detection of missed epilepsy signs on brain MRIs
content:
Researchers from the joint Biomedically‑Informed AI Laboratory of Skoltech—a VEB. RF Group institution—and the University of Sharjah, together with their colleagues, have enhanced computer‑vision algorithms that detect epilepsy and multiple sclerosis on brain MRI scans. The updated neural network goes beyond pixel‑level analysis by also attending to medical features recognized by physicians, while retaining the ability to identify subtle details that can escape human observation.

The developers say the approach could assist doctors in diagnosing these diseases and in choosing appropriate treatment strategies.
summary: Researchers from the joint Biomedically-Informed AI Laboratory of Skoltech (a VEB. RF Group institution) and the University of Sharjah and their colleagues have improved the performance of computer vision algorithms that look for signs of epilepsy and multiple sclerosis on brain MRI scans.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Alpha-emitting radiopharmaceutical therapy well tolerated in early prostate cancer trial
content:
A new alpha‑emitting radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) for advanced prostate cancer was evaluated in an early‑phase trial.  

The trial reported the treatment was well tolerated, observed no dose‑limiting toxicities, and showed encouraging antitumor activity; results were published in The Journal of Nuclear Medicine’s Late‑Breaking Fast Track.
summary: A new alpha-emitting radiopharmaceutical therapy for advanced prostate cancer was well tolerated with no dose‑limiting toxicities observed. The early‑phase trial also reported encouraging signs of antitumor activity and was published in The Journal of Nuclear Medicine's Late‑Breaking Fast Track.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Cochrane review: ergonomics offer no benefit for arm, neck, shoulder pain
content: An updated Cochrane review reports that ergonomic interventions provide no meaningful benefit for pain, function, recovery or sick leave among workers experiencing work‑related arm, neck or shoulder (CANS) complaints, when compared with no treatment.
summary: An updated Cochrane review found ergonomic interventions provide no meaningful benefit for pain, function, recovery or sick leave in workers with work‑related arm, neck or shoulder complaints (CANS). The review compared ergonomic interventions with no treatment and reported no significant improvement.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Focused ultrasound may ease motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease
content:
Stan Au’s Parkinson’s disease has progressed to the point that everyday tasks become difficult. His hands shake so severely he can no longer hold utensils or sign his name, and he has stopped playing pickleball.

He continues to take a widely prescribed medication to manage motor symptoms such as rigidity, stiffness, slow movement, dyskinesia, and tremors.
summary: A noninvasive focused ultrasound treatment is reported to ease motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease. Stan Au's symptoms progressed to severe hand shaking that limited daily tasks despite medication.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Northwestern Kellogg study finds NFL injuries less harmful to team success
content: New research from Northwestern’s Kellogg School of Management indicates that injuries have a smaller impact on NFL team performance than commonly believed. The study notes that, apart from highly paid quarterbacks, losing players—including those with large contracts—does not significantly jeopardize a team’s success.
summary: New research from Northwestern's Kellogg School of Management finds that injury matters less in the NFL than is often assumed. The study says that, with the exception of highly paid quarterbacks, losing even high-dollar players to injury is not as fatal to a team's success.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers Find Why Frogs in Colombia's Sierra Nevada Survive Fungus Outbreak
content:
Amphibians are the most threatened vertebrates on Earth, with 41 % of species facing extinction. In the highlands of Central and South America, a killer fungus has wiped out much of the once‑abundant amphibian diversity.

Yet in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, an isolated mountain range in northern Colombia, amphibians still thrive. The range hosts a remarkable community of at least 48 species, including 25 that are found nowhere else on the planet.
summary: Researchers discovered that frogs in Colombia's Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta have survived the amphibian mass extinction caused by a killer fungus that has wiped out amphibians in the highlands of Central and South America. The mountain range hosts at least 48 amphibian species, 25 of which are endemic to the area.
author: Phys.org

title: UAB-led CONFETI project pilots field urea production using biobatteries and solar power
content:
The CONFETI project, coordinated by the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB), has concluded three years of research with the commissioning of a pilot system that can produce urea directly in the field.  

The system generates the nitrogen fertilizer in an electrochemical reactor that converts carbon dioxide and nitrates into urea, using renewable power supplied by biobatteries and solar panels.
summary: The CONFETI project coordinated by the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona concluded three years of research and commissioned a pilot system that can produce urea directly in the field. The urea is generated in an electrochemical reactor from carbon dioxide and nitrates using renewable energy supplied by biobatteries and solar panels.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers near solution to invasive bramble weed in South Africa
content:
Brambles, invasive alien weeds that have spread across South Africa since the early 1900s, originate from North America and Europe and belong to the genus Rubus. Locally they are known as braam (Afrikaans), ijingijolo (isiZulu) and monoko‑metsi (seSotho).

Researchers are now closer to discovering a natural enemy that could help manage these problematic brambles.
summary: Invasive alien brambles of the genus Rubus have spread across South Africa since the early 1900s after arriving from North America and Europe. Researchers say they are closer to finding a natural enemy to manage the weed, which is called braam, ijingijolo and monoko-metsi locally.
author: Phys.org

title: Northwestern University model tracks 35 Senate races, updating every 10 minutes
content: A new election model from Northwestern University updates predictions every 10 minutes for the 35 U.S. Senate races that are shaping the battle for control, spanning from Alaska to Texas.
summary: From Alaska to Texas, the battle for control of the U. S.
author: Phys.org

title: Review finds digital tech, 3D printing central to circular economy research
content:
A review of research published in the International Journal of Services and Operations Management examined literature from 2020 through 2026 and identified digital technologies, additive manufacturing and resource recovery as the principal themes driving the shift toward a sustainable, circular economy.  

The authors note that advancing this transition will require increased cooperation among businesses and other stakeholders, as well as stronger governmental policies to facilitate progress.
summary: A review of literature from 2020 to 2026 identified digital technologies, additive manufacturing and resource recovery as major themes in the shift toward a sustainable circular economy. The study, published in the International Journal of Services and Operations Management, calls for greater business‑stakeholder cooperation and improved government policies to support the transition.
author: Phys.org

title: MapInsights helps University of Illinois trainees as guards become community officers
content: MapInsights is being used to help police trainees learn the territory. In early 2026, the University of Illinois Division of Public Safety faced a challenge: it planned to convert 11 security guards into community service officers, shifting them from a single building to covering an entire beat.
summary: In early 2026 the University of Illinois Division of Public Safety planned to convert 11 security guards to community service officers. The conversion would move them from a single‑building assignment to covering an entire beat, and MapInsights helps police trainees learn the territory.
author: Phys.org

title: Asteroid that killed dinosaurs may have aided ants' rise via jumping genes
content: Scientists suggest that the asteroid impact that ended the dinosaurs may have paved the way for ants to dominate the planet. Research shows bursts of activity from mobile genetic elements—“jumping genes”—coincided with the emergence of major ant lineages and may have enhanced their sophisticated chemical communication.
summary: The asteroid that killed the dinosaurs may have set the stage for ants to conquer the planet, with a surprising boost from “jumping genes” hidden in their DNA.
author: Science Daily

title: McGill researchers find T cells sense tissue stiffness to guide memory formation
content:
Scientists at McGill University reported that immune cells possess a previously unknown ability. Their research shows T cells can detect the stiffness of surrounding tissues and use these physical signals to influence whether they become long‑lasting memory cells that protect against future infections.  

The discovery could reshape understanding of long‑term immunity.
summary: Scientists at McGill University discovered that T cells can detect the stiffness of surrounding tissues. This physical sensing helps determine whether the T cells develop into long‑lasting memory cells that protect against future infections.
author: Science Daily

title: The autistic brain processes faces differently than scientists thought
content: A new study reports that autistic children’s brains process faces differently, and that these differences may emerge earlier than previously believed. Researchers observed that brain signals linked to face recognition become increasingly specialized in neurotypical children as they age, whereas autistic children exhibit far less change in these signals over time. The findings suggest a possible neural basis for the challenges some autistic individuals face in recognizing faces and interpreting emotions.
summary: A major new study reveals that autistic children’s brains process faces differently, and those differences may begin earlier than scientists previously thought. Researchers found that brain signals associated with recognizing faces become more specialized as neurotypical children grow older, but show much less change in autistic children.
author: Science Daily

title: Daily fiber supplement cuts knee osteoarthritis pain and boosts strength in trial
content: A new clinical trial found that a simple daily fiber supplement significantly reduced knee osteoarthritis pain, enhanced muscle strength and lowered pain sensitivity. Researchers reported that the observed benefits appear to be associated with alterations in gut bacteria and the hormone GLP‑1, suggesting a potential new strategy for arthritis relief.
summary: A new clinical trial found that a simple daily fiber supplement significantly reduced knee osteoarthritis pain and improved muscle strength. Researchers said the effects may be related to changes in gut bacteria and the hormone GLP‑1, suggesting a new approach to arthritis relief.

title: Chiricahua National Park redesignated from monument in October 2026
content: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory The Land of the Standing-Up Rocks Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Some 27 million years ago, a volcano in what’s now southeastern Arizona unleashed a spectacular series of eruptions, strewing more than 1,000 times as much volcanic material across the landscape as Mount St. Helens did in 1980. The explosive eruptions blanketed the region, part of the Chiricahua Apache Nation’s traditional lands, with ash and pumice. Layered into this were massive pyroclastic flows that hardened into deposits of welded rhyolitic tuff that in some areas were nearly 1,600 feet (500 meters) thick, about three times the height of the Washington Monument. As the magma chamber emptied, the ground above it collapsed, leaving a gaping depression—the Turkey Creek caldera —that was roughly 12 miles (19 kilometers) wide and 4,900 feet (1,500 meters) deep. An array of geologic processes, including erosion and weathering, gradually sculpted the welded layer of tuff into the collection of dramatic spires, hoodoos, and canyons that visitors to the caldera area encounter today. The Apache called the area “ The Land of the Standing-Up Rocks ” for good reason. Hiking through Rhyolite Canyon or driving through Bonita Canyon means encountering a dizzying maze of rock pinnacles, some hundreds of feet tall. Others, like Big Balanced Rock, have surprisingly large boulders precariously perched on top. Meanwhile, those at Heart of Rocks and Massai Point are gathered into groups of hundreds. The area was designated a national monument in 1924 to preserve its remarkable geology. In October 2026, it was redesignated as Chiricahua National Park (pronounced cheery-cow-ah ). The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured this cloud-free image of the new national park on July 2, 2026. Individual rock spires are too small to distinguish, but the eroding rhyolitic tuff landscape appears gray. Stream valleys dense with trees and other vegetation, including Rhyolite Canyon and Bonita Canyon, snake across the landscape. With four biogeographic regions converging in the park—the Sonoran Desert, the Chihuahuan Desert, the Rocky Mountains, and the Sierra Madre—it is a haven of plant diversity. Among the 1,000 species growing within the park’s varied desert, grassland, chaparral, deciduous forest, and coniferous forest ecosystems are agaves, prickly pear cacti, yuccas, manzanita, pine, fir, cypress, sycamore, juniper, and oak. The park’s location within the Chiricahua Mountains puts it among several “ sky islands ” in Arizona—isolated mountain ranges that emerge from the surrounding desert “sea.” According to the National Park Service, the range’s highest point (outside the park) rises 2,986 meters (9,795 feet) above sea level, more than 1,800 meters above the surrounding valley. title: APOD shows mutual occultation of Jupiter’s moons Ganymede and Io on Oct 20, 2026
content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 28 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Michael Wong The Mutual Occultation of Ganymede and Io Explanation: Jupiter is one of the least lonely planets in the Solar System, at least when it comes to natural satellites. 115 moons have been discovered orbiting Jupiter so far! ( Saturn has the most with 293, but who’s counting. ) Ganymede and Io, two of Jupiter’s Galilean moons, met in the sky on October 20th, 2026. Today’s video captures the meeting, with Ganymede briefly blocking Io from view. This event, when an astronomical object passes in front of another and either completely or partially blocks it, is called a mutual occultation. The mutual occultations of Galilean moons are rare to witness because they require Earth’s edge-on view of their orbits. This occurs once every 6 years when Jupiter reaches its equinox and appears less “tilted”. Ganymede is also casting its shadow on Jupiter’s right side. Any fictional Jovian species within the shadow would experience a solar eclipse! title: Rights groups oppose UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh's UN secretary general bid amid Sudan claims
content: Human rights groups urged countries to reject UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh’s bid to become UN secretary‑general, citing allegations that Abu Dhabi funds Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. The UAE denies these accusations. Nusseibeh, 48, is seeking to become the first woman to lead the United Nations.
summary: Human rights groups urged countries to reject UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh’s bid to become UN secretary general, citing allegations that Abu Dhabi funds Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. Nusseibeh, 48, seeks to become the first woman to lead the United Nations, while the UAE denies the accusations.

title: Israel exit polls show Netanyahu and Eisenkot blocs tied, both short of majority
content: Both blocs would fall short of the 61 seats needed to form a government as support for Palestinian parties surges Full report: Israel election too close to call as exit polls give Netanyahu bloc slightly fewer seats Analysis: Rise of Palestinian parties in Knesset will redraw Israel’s political landscape Israel election: what we know so far A record number of Israeli’s are expected to have voted at “special polling stations” in 2026, casting more confusion into the mix as the results as these ballots are not expected to be announced before Thursday. Under Israeli electoral law, each voter is assigned to a specific polling station and can only vote at that station. However in exceptional circumstances, some voters are allowed to cast their ballot at special polling stations they are not registered at. Among those afforded this exception are soldiers stationed at IDF bases, diplomats working abroad, prisoners and prison guards and people in hospital.
summary: Exit polls indicate the Netanyahu bloc and the Eisenkot bloc are tied and each falls short of the 61 seats required to form a government, with support for Palestinian parties rising. A record number of Israelis voted at special polling stations in 2026, and those results are not expected to be announced before Thursday.
author: Guardian World

title: Gulf states push multipart peace deal to reopen Hormuz Strait, pull Houthis from Yemen
content:
Gulf states are negotiating a multipart peace deal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within four days of lifting sanctions on Iran and secure a substantial withdrawal of Houthi forces inside Yemen. The plan is presented as a means to prevent what the Gulf states describe as a disastrous renewal of war between the United States and Iran.  

The United States has been informed of the talks’ progress but is waiting for a concession, which European powers say could involve Iran permitting United Nations weapons inspectors to return to the country.
summary: Gulf states push multipart peace deal to reopen Hormuz Strait, pull Houthis from Yemen.
author: Guardian World

title: Australia’s inflation climbs to 4.3%, boosting expectations of another rate hike
content:
Australia’s headline consumer price index rose to 4.3%, according to the latest CPI release. The Reserve Bank of Australia’s preferred “underlying” inflation measure, which excludes volatile items, registered an annual 3.6% increase to September. The data were released ahead of the Reserve Bank’s monetary‑policy decision scheduled for next week.

The rise in both headline and underlying inflation has heightened expectations that the central bank may implement a fifth interest‑rate increase this year, as the cost‑of‑living pressure intensifies amid the ongoing Middle East conflict.
summary: Australia’s inflation climbs to 4.3%, boosting expectations of another rate hike.

title: UEFI firmware flaw in TianoCore EDK II affects global servers
content:
A critical code-execution vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-97631, has been discovered in the TianoCore EDK II, an open-source codebase used to create UEFI firmware for boot-time sequences. This memory-corruption flaw, which carries a severity rating of 9.5 out of 10, resides in an ICMP component and affects virtually all UEFI suppliers, including AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix, as well as Microsoft’s Project Mu. The UEFI Forum previously described EDK II as the "preeminent solution" for UEFI specifications, highlighting its widespread adoption by hardware makers and cloud providers.

The vulnerability allows attackers to execute malicious code before the operating system and firmware can activate defenses such as Secure Boot, which establishes a chain of trust for code loaded during boot, including the Trusted Platform Module (TPM). Although the final payloads delivered by this specific flaw lack persistence and run only once, they provide a significant opening for attackers to install other payloads that execute early in the boot process. This issue presents a major challenge for defenders responding to the vulnerability across global server vendors and data centers.
summary: A high-severity memory-corruption vulnerability in the TianoCore EDK II codebase allows attackers to execute malicious code before operating system defenses activate. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-97631 and impacts UEFI suppliers including AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix.

title: China's top-secret spaceplane can't hide in low-Earth orbit

The photograph was taken by Vantor, a company formerly known as Maxar, which provides reconnaissance imagery to the US military and intelligence agencies. While these satellites are primarily used for Earth imaging, they can also direct their telescopes toward objects in space.

The captured image reveals that the Chinese spaceplane features delta wings, payload bay doors, a dark heat shield, and a rear-mounted service module equipped with power-generating solar arrays. According to the report, the design of this winged vessel is, to a significant degree, a copy of the X-37B spaceplane operated by the US Space Force.

title: Washington state health officials detail 5 measles importations from South Carolina
content:

These introductions resulted in 26 cases among Washington residents before health officials contained the spread. The findings highlight that domestic travel now poses a greater risk than international incursions, particularly as nationwide vaccination rates have declined and domestic outbreaks have become more frequent.

The South Carolina outbreak, which began on October 2, 2025, and ended on April 26, 2026, confirmed 997 cases. However, the article notes that an ongoing outbreak in Pennsylvania has since surpassed the South Carolina total.

title: Israel election too close to call as exit polls show Netanyahu bloc slightly behind
content:
Early indications after Israel’s election suggest that the composition of the new government will not be clear for some time. Voter turnout was described as historic, with a record level of participation by Israeli Arab voters, and the election has been called one of the most consequential in the country’s history.

Exit polls released on Tuesday evening showed that the opposition bloc of parties led by former Israel Defense Forces chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot was projected to win a slight majority of Knesset seats, edging out the right‑ and far‑right coalition associated with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Despite this projection, Netanyahu’s Likud party emerged as the single largest party in the vote.

The results also point to a rise in Palestinian parties within the Knesset, a development that could reshape Israel’s political landscape. No definitive winner has been declared, and further clarification of the governing coalition remains pending.
summary: The vote saw a historic turnout and record participation by Israeli Arab voters, leaving no clear winner. Exit polls indicated the opposition bloc led by former IDF chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot would win slightly more seats than Benjamin Netanyahu’s right‑wing coalition, though Likud remained the largest party.

title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
content: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago. That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way. What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart. Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf. But on rare occasions, the supernova doesn't completely destroy the star, and a shattered stellar body remains, called a zombie star. These events are called Type Iax supernovas. Pa 30 was first identified in 2013 by a citizen scientist in 2013, but scientists soon linked it to a cosmic explosion recorded independently in the year 1181 in Japanese, Chinese, and Arabic historical documentation. That makes this one of only five supernovas seen before the invention of the telescope. "Reliable historical records of stellar explosions extend back only about a thousand years. For all we know, there might well be similar remnants still lurking in the dark in our own galaxy," team member Ilaria Caiazzo, assistant professor at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA), said in a statement. "Today, we are lucky to study an intriguing object we know was observed by astronomers who made three independent historical records of the event centuries before the invention of the telescope." Solar system-sized pearls Pa 30 is a good laboratory to study supernovas because, at around 7,500 light-years away, it is relatively close to Earth on cosmic scales. For instance, the heart of our galaxy is around 26,000 light-years away. "We can see this much detail because of Pa 30's proximity to Earth," said Caiazzo. "This proximity makes Pa 30 uniquely valuable for study." It is also an important subject of study because it is the only supernova remnant in which we can see a zombie star. Using the Gemini North telescope, Caiazzo and colleagues zoomed in on Pa 30, discovering knots along the strands of gas radiating out from the site of the cosmic explosion, like pearls on a string. These pearls are each wide enough to encompass the orbit of Neptune, the most distant planet from the sun, ten times over. "The planetary region of our solar system could fit in each knot about ten times with room to spare," said Caiazzo. "The knots are quite strikingly uniform. We are excited to try to model them." The team also discovered that the zombie star sits almost perfectly at the heart of Pa 30. When these cosmic explosions happen, they should provide any debris, including zombie stars, with a kick. The fact that this "living dead" star still sits dead center of this wreckage suggests that when this explosion happened, it was roughly symmetrical and the kick was relatively light. "Explosions conserve momentum. If the explosion itself was perfectly symmetric, the ejecta should also be symmetric, and the surviving star should not receive a substantial kick," Caiazzo said. "We were able to measure a precise upper limit of the remnant star's transverse kick speed, showing that it was surprisingly small. We practically don't see the star moving away at all." An image of the nebula Pa 30. (Image credit: Robert Fesen) While there are still many mysteries surrounding Pa 30 and its zombie occupant, one of the most exciting prospects emerging from this research is the possibility it will help identify the wreckage of other Type Iax supernovas in our galaxy. "While we can see Type Iax supernovas in distant galaxies as point sources of light, resolving the remnants of such explosions is only possible in our own galaxy and in very few nearby ones," Caiazzo concluded. "Eventually, we plan to use Pa 30's distinctive properties to search the Milky Way and nearby galaxies for similar objects." The team's research was published in The Astrophysical Journal.
summary: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart.

title: Macklemore’s Free Palestine tour debuts in Dublin with Hozier, Kneecap
content:
Macklemore’s Free Palestine tour achieved a sold-out status at Dublin’s 13,000-capacity 3Arena, marking the first European date of the benefit concert series. The event featured several unannounced guests, including performances by Hozier and Kneecap, as well as video messages from Mark Ruffalo and Cynthia Nixon. During the show, a member of Kneecap humorously thanked Ed Sheeran for organizing the concert, a comment that reflected the complex history between the artists.

The tour emerged after Macklemore was removed from Sheeran’s summer US tour following a speech about Palestine at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium. This removal occurred after Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots, pressured Sheeran to drop the rapper. In response to the controversy, all other artists on Sheeran’s tour quit in solidarity, leaving his own tour to continue amid significant criticism.

Macklemore leveraged the increased publicity from the incident to launch his own tour in larger venues than his previous European dates. The proceeds from these sold-out shows are donated to organizations assisting Palestinians.
summary: The first European date of Macklemore’s sold-out benefit tour featured unannounced guests including Hozier, Kneecap, and video messages from Mark Ruffalo and Cynthia Nixon. The concert took place at Dublin’s 3Arena, with proceeds donated to organisations assisting Palestinians.

title: The Nerves: The Hit-Free Band Behind Blondie's 'Hanging on the Telephone'
content:
The Nerves, a trio formed in 1974 consisting of Jack Lee, Peter Case, and Paul Collins, developed a reputation for crafting short, melodic songs with a intense work ethic. Despite their dedication and shared stages with bands like Devo and the Ramones during a nationwide tour, the music industry largely ignored them. In response, the group pressed their own EP and continued to gig extensively, aiming to create their own opportunities within the music scene.

The band’s brief career ended with a split in 1978, followed by an unexpected posthumous association with a major hit. Blondie’s third album, Parallel Lines, opened with a cover version of the Nerves’ song “Hanging on the Telephone.” While this track had previously been a signature piece for the trio, the successful Blondie cover effectively obscured the Nerves’ history, leading to a narrative where their own contributions were overshadowed by the later fame of the cover version.
summary: The Nerves, a trio formed in 1974, wrote the song "Hanging on the Telephone" which became a signature track for Blondie. The band split in 1978 after the music industry ignored them, despite their songwriting brilliance and touring with groups like Devo and the Ramones.

title: 1.9-Million-Year-Old Discovery Rewrites Human Evolution Story
content: New evidence indicates that early humans reached the Jordan Valley at least 1.9 million years ago, hundreds of thousands of years earlier than previously estimated. Advanced dating methods show the ‘Ubeidiya site is roughly as old as the Dmanisi site in Georgia, positioning both among the earliest known human settlements outside Africa.
summary: New evidence indicates that early humans reached the Jordan Valley at least 1.9 million years ago, which is hundreds of thousands of years earlier than previously thought. Advanced dating methods revealed that the 'Ubeidiya site is roughly as old as the Dmanisi site in Georgia, placing both among the earliest known human settlements outside Africa.
author: Science Daily

title: Wall squats twice weekly linked to lower blood pressure in 100 adults
content: A study involving 100 adults indicates that wall squats performed one or two times per week can help maintain significant reductions in systolic blood pressure over the short term. This simple exercise routine offers a potential method for lowering blood pressure without the need for daily workouts or expensive equipment.
summary: A study of 100 adults found that performing wall squats once or twice a week helped maintain significant reductions in systolic blood pressure. This simple exercise routine requires no daily workouts or expensive equipment.
author: Science Daily

title: Mayo Clinic finds new methods to target aging ‘zombie’ cells, including tomato compound
content:
Mayo Clinic scientists have published seven studies detailing new insights into “zombie cells,” which are aging cells that persist in the body and contribute to inflammation and disease. These findings identify new strategies for targeting these cells, including the use of a natural compound found in tomatoes. The research reveals why these lingering cells are harmful to overall health.

In experimental treatments involving aging mice, these new strategies successfully reduced inflammation and improved both physical and brain health. The study suggests that these discoveries could pave the way for future therapies designed to combat specific biological processes associated with aging.
summary: Mayo Clinic scientists have uncovered surprising new insights into “zombie cells,” aging cells that linger in the body and contribute to inflammation and disease. Seven studies reveal why these cells are harmful and identify new strategies for targeting them, including a natural compound found in tomatoes.
author: Science Daily

title: BAE Systems Inspects NASA NEO Surveyor's 20-Foot Sunshade
content:
BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems released an image on Oct. 26, 2026, showing a technician inspecting the large sunshade for NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor mission. The structure stands 20 feet (6 meters) tall and measures 8 feet (2.4 meters) wide at its base. This component is designed to keep the mission’s infrared space telescope cool while simultaneously providing power to the spacecraft.

The NEO Surveyor is intended to detect difficult-to-find near-Earth asteroids and comets, including those located in the direction of the Sun. This specific region of the sky presents challenges for ground-based optical telescopes, making the space-based infrared capability essential for these searches.
summary: A technician inspected the 20-foot-tall sunshade for NASA's Near-Earth Object Surveyor mission, which measures 8 feet wide at its base. The structure will keep the infrared telescope cool and provide power as it searches for near-Earth asteroids and comets.
author: NASA News

title: 28-Year-Old DOGE Operative Jeremy Lewin Oversaw USAID Destruction, HR Says No Record
content: A 28‑year‑old DOGE operative named Jeremy Lewin, who was not recorded as having been onboarded by USAID’s HR, allegedly oversaw the destruction of the agency. It remains unclear whether Lewin had legal authority to carry out those actions.
summary: Jeremy Lewin, a 28-year-old DOGE operative, oversaw the destruction of USAID. The agency's human resources department said he had not been onboarded and it is unclear whether he had legal authority to do so.
author: Wired

title: Anthropic designs unique governance structure to balance IPO with AI safety
content:
Anthropic plans to pursue an Initial Public Offering while maintaining its commitment to safe AI development, a strategy designed to balance access to public market funds with its core mission. The company acknowledges that increased model capabilities pose greater risks and that shareholders seeking returns may lack patience for safety measures that delay product launches. This approach contrasts with OpenAI, whose CEO Sam Altman cited investor pressures as a reason for not pursuing an IPO this year.

To mitigate potential conflicts between profit expectations and safety priorities, Anthropic intends to implement a complex governance structure. This framework is designed to help the company resist investor pressures that could compromise its safety standards, allowing it to navigate the transition to public markets without sacrificing its stated ethical objectives.
summary: Anthropic is preparing for an IPO while seeking to maintain its mission of developing AI safely without compromising for shareholder returns. The company intends to use a complex governance structure to resist investor pressure that might prioritize speed over safety measures.
author: The Verge

title: Trump administration to weaken methane leak rules for oil and gas companies
content:
The Trump administration is expected to announce plans to weaken regulations designed to prevent methane leaks from oil and gas operations. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) intends to undo Biden-era rules as part of President Donald Trump’s broader deregulatory agenda. Methane, the primary component of natural gas, is described as a smog-forming pollutant and a powerful greenhouse gas that is up to 80 times as potent as carbon dioxide over a 20-year horizon.

This move represents a reversal of previous EPA efforts to address routine leaks from wells and pipelines. The administration frames the regulatory changes as a benefit for the fossil fuel industry, shifting policy away from the stricter standards established during the prior administration.
summary: Trump administration to weaken methane leak rules for oil and gas companies.
author: The Verge

title: Elon Musk says Ukraine’s military violated Starlink’s terms of service
content: Elon Musk claims Ukraine violated Starlink's terms of service before the recent slowdown, as reported earlier by Ars Technica. According to Musk, "Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week," however Ukrainian officials have denied that happened, or that it is actually possible for them to do. The statement comes nearly two weeks after Ukrainian officials accused SpaceX of putting limits on the military's satellite internet service that disrupted its drone missions and operations. As reported by Axios, Ukraine uses Starlink for communications …
summary: Elon Musk says Ukraine’s military violated Starlink’s terms of service.
author: The Verge

title: Evernote Raises Subscription Prices from $130 to $250
content:
Evernote, the long‑standing note‑taking app, announced a significant revision to its subscription structure earlier this year. The change forces some users to move from paying $130 per year to $250 for the same level of service.

According to the announcement, the app’s highest tier now costs more than 3.3 times the price of the most advanced tier that existed in 2023. It also represents a ten‑fold increase over the annual subscription fees that Evernote charged from its 2008 launch through 2016.

The price hike has prompted users to reassess the value they place on the app’s features and to consider whether the new cost aligns with their usage and needs.
summary: Evernote changed its subscription tiers, raising the highest tier from $130 per year to $250. The new price is more than 3.3 times the most advanced tier in 2023 and ten times the price charged between 2008 and 2016.
author: Ars Technica

title: DeepMind unveils Genie 4 world model with realistic physics and humans
content:
Google DeepMind has announced the release of its new world‑model, Genie 4, following the 2023 launch of Genie 3 that had caused a sharp drop in gaming‑industry stocks. The company says Genie 4 improves on Genie 3 in almost every way and that, if a customer pays the required fee, the model could be available for use sooner than expected. While the output of Genie 4 can resemble a video game—an aspect that led to concerns about Genie 3—DeepMind does not view the technology from that perspective.

According to Google, world models are a key step toward artificial general intelligence. A world model builds a virtual world without the need to pre‑render environments or program interactive elements. Users simply describe what they want, and the model generates the experience frame by frame in real time. DeepMind claims the technology could provide endless training environments for physical robots or enable rapid prototyping in creative fields, provided the simulations are accurate. The improvements in Genie 4 are attributed in part to Google’s updated Gemini models.
summary: DeepMind released Genie 4, an updated world model that improves on Genie 3 with more realistic physics and human simulations. The model can generate virtual environments in real time, offering infinite training settings for robots and rapid prototyping for creative fields, thanks to its integration with updated Gemini models.
author: Ars Technica

title: Ford simplifies using your EV as a home battery with the $30K Fathom
content:
Ford announced that the forthcoming Fathom, a sub‑$30,000 electric pickup truck slated for release next year, will include built‑in vehicle‑to‑home technology. Unlike the now‑discontinued F‑150 Lightning, which relied on a wallbox inverter to convert DC power from the vehicle into AC for the home, the Fathom’s inverter is integrated into the truck itself. This design means every Fathom will be able to function as a backup battery for a household.

The company’s reveal comes amid a broader shift toward affordable electric trucks. Ford’s Fathom is priced about $5,000 higher than a competing “Blank Slate” pickup from a new startup. The Slate is marketed as a bare‑bones two‑door vehicle that omits an onboard modem, touchscreens, and an infotainment system, focusing on the features the internet suggests consumers want.

In contrast, the Fathom offers additional doors, a modern infotainment system, CarPlay, electric windows, and access to Ford’s extensive dealership network. These extras may appeal to buyers who value service convenience, especially given Ford’s history of frequent recalls.
summary: Ford simplifies using your EV as a home battery with the $30K Fathom.
author: Ars Technica

title: Warner Bros. releases final trailer for Dune: Part Three
content:
Warner Bros. has released the final trailer for Dune: Part Three, the last film in Denis Villeneuve’s adaptation of Frank Herbert’s novels. The new clip arrives ahead of the pre‑Christmas release of the movie.

The action‑packed trailer focuses on the iconic anti‑hero Paul Atreides, portrayed by Timothée Chalamet, and sets up the film’s final act. It follows the momentum built in earlier promotional material, including a broody extended teaser in March and a July trailer that packed in hints and Easter eggs for fans of the books.

A brief recap of the first two films shows that 2021’s Dune ended with the brutal defeat of House Atreides by rival House Harkonnen. Paul and his mother, Lady Jessica (Rebecca Ferguson), flee to the desert and take refuge among the Fremen, where Paul meets Chani (Zendaya), a woman he has been seeing in visions.
summary: Warner Bros. releases final trailer for Dune: Part Three.
author: Ars Technica

title: China team releases natural-language protein design tool
content:
Protein‑design software is becoming more powerful, yet it still demands a deep understanding of protein structure. Users must specify details such as the exact positions of amino acids involved in enzyme mechanisms and the water molecules present in the catalytic site. Once these parameters are set, the software can generate the remainder of the protein around the target.

A large collaboration of researchers in China has developed a new tool that accepts natural‑language prompts to produce proteins with a user‑specified function. While the success rate for producing fully functional proteins is modest, the team reports that the tool can still deliver usable designs.

Separately, Hugging Face announced that it now hosts a similar tool for DNA‑level design. The combination of natural‑language input and automated design—sometimes called “vibe coding”—may bring protein design to a broader audience, provided users have laboratory resources to evaluate and refine the resulting proteins.
summary: A collaboration of researchers in China has released a protein design tool that accepts natural language prompts to generate proteins with specified functions. Hugging Face also announced a similar DNA‑level design tool, though the new protein tool's success rate is modest and requires lab validation to separate good designs from failures.
author: Ars Technica

title: Google opens applications for Android Registered App Stores program launching Dec. 1
content:
Google has announced that its Android Registered App Stores program will officially launch on December 1, and applications to join the program are now open. The program follows a court‑ordered requirement that U.S. users have access to app stores within Google Play, while international users can participate through Google’s voluntary program.

Stores that are accepted into the program will receive preferential treatment on the Android platform. Users of approved stores will be able to install apps with a single click, mirroring the Play Store experience, and the stores will also be permitted to update apps silently in the background.

A Google spokesperson noted that the program was first announced in March to give third‑party app stores a more streamlined way to reach users while maintaining the safety and security of the Android ecosystem. Eligible app stores outside the U.S. can now apply to register their stores ahead of the new simplified installation experience that will roll out to users later this year.
summary: Google announced that third‑party app stores outside the United States can now apply to its Registered App Stores program, which will launch on Dec. 1. Accepted stores will receive preferential treatment on Android, enabling single‑click installs and silent background updates, with support rolling out to some devices later this year.
author: Ars Technica

title: Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly left Brazil for US after election defeat
content: According to a police source cited by AFP, Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports have been cancelled and there is no formal record of his departure from Brazil, despite reports that he has left for the United States after his election defeat.
summary: Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly left Brazil for the United States after an election defeat. A police source told AFP his passports had been cancelled and there was no formal record of his departure.

content: Thomas van Tonder, suspended beneath South Africa’s 216‑metre‑high Bloukrans Bridge, crossed 600 monkey bars that spanned more than 280 metres. He completed the challenge in 47 minutes and 37 seconds.
summary: Thomas van Tonder was suspended beneath South Africa's 216‑metre‑high Bloukrans Bridge and crossed 600 monkey bars spanning more than 280 metres. He completed the challenge in 47 minutes and 37 seconds.

title: Qatar urges Iran to end threats and reopen Strait of Hormuz
content: Regional powers are seeking a way out of the Iran war as attacks threaten shipping and energy supplies. Qatar says mediation continues after a visit to Tehran, where Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey have also held talks with Iranian leaders.
summary: Qatar said it is continuing mediation after a visit to Tehran and urged Iran to show goodwill by ending threats to the region and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Regional powers including Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey have also held talks with Iranian leaders as attacks threaten shipping and energy supplies.

title: Egyptian parliament approves military aid to Saudi Arabia if requested amid Houthi attacks
content: Egypt’s parliament voted to approve military assistance for Saudi Arabia if requested, citing Houthi attacks that threaten the kingdom and Red Sea shipping. The decision follows Saudi officials holding talks in Iran as part of regional efforts to prevent further escalation of the conflict.
summary: Egypt's parliament approved military help for Saudi Arabia if requested as Houthi attacks threaten the kingdom and Red Sea shipping. The vote came as Saudi officials held talks in Iran amid regional efforts to prevent further escalation.

title: Exit polls show no clear winner in Israeli election as Netanyahu urges voters
content: Exit polls indicate that no party has emerged as a clear winner in the Israeli election. Amid the uncertainty, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has spent much of the day urging his supporters to go to the polls, describing the contest as a “matter of life and death.”
summary: Exit polls indicate there is no clear victor in the Israeli election. Netanyahu spent much of the day urging supporters to vote, describing the election as a matter of life and death.

title: Israel election turnout hits 55% by 4 p.m., highest in decades
content:
Israeli voters turned out at record levels, reaching 55 % by 4 pm local time on Tuesday, October 27.  

The turnout, described as unseen in decades, reflects a deeply divided electorate weighing a verdict on veteran right‑wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the first election held since the October 7, 2023 attack. FRANCE24’s Kethevane Gorjestani reports further details.
summary: Israelis flocked to the polls Tuesday (October 27) in turnout unseen in decades, with a deeply divided electorate delivering a verdict on veteran right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the first election since the October 7, 2023 attack. FRANCE24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.
author: France 24

title: Israelis vote in tense election seen as referendum on Netanyahu's leadership
content: Israelis voted on Tuesday, Oct. 27, in a tense national election widely viewed as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s leadership since the Hamas‑led Oct. 7, 2023 attack on Israel and the wars that have since shaken the Middle East.
summary: Israelis were voting Tuesday (October 27) in a tense national election widely seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership since the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel and the wars that have since shaken the Middle East.

content: French lawmakers observed a minute of silence for Pengo Bossio Wangi, who died last week in a shooting described as a racist attack. The incident also wounded at least five other individuals, including a 12-year-old girl.
summary: French lawmakers held a minute of silence for Pengo Bossio Wangi, who died in a racist shooting last week. At least five other people were wounded in the attack, including a 12‑year‑old girl, according to FRANCE 24’s Claire Paccalin.

title: French proposal to make rioters pay damages criticized as anti-democratic
content:
Rights groups have criticized a proposed French law, arguing that it is anti‑democratic and could undermine the legitimate right to protest. The bill would hold rioters liable to pay thousands of euros for any damage they cause.

The government introduced the measure to curb looting and vandalism that has accompanied ongoing national protests. Those protests are driven by concerns over poor conditions in French schools and the high cost of living.
summary: Critics say the proposed French law that would require rioters to pay thousands of euros for damage is anti‑democratic because it could undermine the right to protest. The government introduced the measure to curb looting and vandalism linked to ongoing national protests over school conditions and the cost of living.
author: France 24

title: Israeli election seen as referendum on Netanyahu, security and democracy, says expert
content: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Ron Gerlitz, CEO of aChord Center at Hebrew University, an Israeli organization specialising in the social psychology of intergroup relations. “The main issue in this election is the fight for Israeli democracy,” explains Gerlitz. And beneath the struggle over democratic institutions lies the erosion of Benjamin Netanyahu's longstanding association with national security. Gerlitz also examines the psychological foundations of Netanyahu's enduring support, the influence of conspiracy narratives, the electoral significance of Arab parties and the uncertain future of the two-state solution.
summary: Ron Gerlitz, CEO of aChord Center at Hebrew University, said the main issue in the election is the fight for Israeli democracy. He added that the election also reflects erosion of Benjamin Netanyahu's link to national security and involves topics such as conspiracy narratives, Arab parties' significance and the two‑state solution's future.
author: France 24

title: Student assemblies' list defeats Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party Sunday
content: Serbia’s student assemblies selected a slate of academics, engineers, artists and activists who defeated President Aleksandar Vucic’s right‑wing Serbian Progressive Party on Sunday. The win follows nearly two years of student‑led anti‑corruption protests and is seen as a potential model for movements that aim to convert street demonstrations into tangible political change.
summary: A list of academics, engineers, artists and activists chosen by Serbia’s student assemblies defeated long‑ruling president Aleksandar Vucic's right‑wing Serbian Progressive Party on Sunday. The shock victory came after nearly two years of student‑led anti‑corruption protests.
author: France 24

title: Ibrahim Abu Ahmad says Arab citizens need Jewish ally in Israeli election
content: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Ibrahim Abu Ahmad, Author, Palestinian Israeli political and peace activist and Head of Social Media for Israel's left-wing Democrats. “Currently, the sentiment in Israel is built around fear and trauma,” explains Ahmad. His most striking observation concerns the apparent contradiction between political leadership and public sentiment: “Many want to see an Arab-Jewish coalition. It's the leadership that is afraid to say it.” Ultimately, he moves beyond conventional electoral calculations to frame Arab-Jewish partnership as a question of democratic survival.
summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Ibrahim Abu Ahmad, Author, Palestinian Israeli political and peace activist and Head of Social Media for Israel's left-wing Democrats. “Currently, the sentiment in Israel is built around fear and trauma,” explains Ahmad.
author: France 24

title: Netanyahu government accused of attacking Israel's judicial system and democracy
content:
Annette Young introduced Alain Greilsammer, a professor of political science at Bar‑Ilan University in Tel Aviv, to discuss Israel’s current political climate. Greilsammer noted that the October 7 attacks, regional tensions with Iran and deepening domestic divisions have placed democratic accountability, judicial independence and the unequal distribution of civic obligations at the forefront of the upcoming election.

He warned that Prime Minister Netanyahu’s policies could steer Israel toward “something like an authoritarian or non‑democratic state.” Greilsammer added that Arab political parties may play a decisive role in shaping the election’s outcome.
summary: Alain Greilsammer, a professor of political science at Bar‑Ilan University, said the upcoming election will be driven by concerns about democratic accountability, judicial independence and unequal civic obligations. He warned that Netanyahu’s policies could turn Israel into an authoritarian‑like state and said Arab parties might play a decisive role in the election outcome.
author: France 24

title: US Reopens Talks with Myanmar Junta as EU's Boycott Faces Scrutiny
content: The United States has begun reopening talks with Myanmar’s military‑backed government, while a number of Southeast Asian nations are also restarting diplomatic contacts with the junta. In response, the European Union is confronting questions about its ongoing boycott of the Myanmar military regime.
summary: The United States has reopened talks with Myanmar's military-backed government. Several Southeast Asian nations have resumed diplomatic contacts, prompting the European Union to confront questions about its boycott of the junta.

title: RAF Fairford petrol van plot linked to handler alleged to work for Iran
content:
Two men have been charged under the National Security Act after a Westminster magistrates’ court heard they were directed by a handler identified as “Ali,” whom police say was acting on behalf of Iranian intelligence. The prosecution said Ali instructed a group to drive vans loaded with petrol to RAF Fairford.

According to prosecutors, one of the five drivers called police in the early hours of 27 September after Ali warned the group that a bomb had been placed in the vans. The court was informed that the warning prompted the call to authorities.
summary: RAF Fairford petrol van plot linked to handler alleged to work for Iran.
author: Guardian World

title: Unpaid carers say chancellor’s plan to scrap carer allowance cliff edge falls short
content: Digital taper system for benefit expected in budget, but those already hit with overpayments will still have to pay “On the surface it sounds really positive – and I really hope that it is,” says unpaid carer Guy Shahar of the government’s decision to abolish the notorious carer’s allowance cliff edge. But Shahar is angry that most carers hit with unjust overpayments in the past will still have to repay them, for all the promise of a different future. And he notes that the cliff edge remains in place for four more years, potentially catching out more carers.
summary: Unpaid carer Guy Shahar said the chancellor’s decision to abolish the carer’s allowance cliff edge sounds positive but falls short. He warned that carers who have already received overpayments must still repay them and that the cliff edge will remain for four more years, potentially affecting more carers.
author: Guardian World

title: Israel election day opens with minute of silence by 7 Oct victims' families
content: Bereaved families tell voters to remember the victims while others have flown thousands of miles to cast their ballots Election day in Israel began with a protest by some of the voters with most at stake. Bereaved families of those killed in the 7 October attacks held a minute of silence at 6.29 am, the moment when Hamas launched its onslaught just over three years ago. They gathered in a Tel Aviv plaza that has become known as “hostages square” because it was the centre of demonstrations demanding the return of more than 200 captives from Gaza. Holding pictures of their loved ones, they stood in silence then called on voters to remember the losses and betrayals of that day when deciding on the next government.
summary: Israel election day opens with minute of silence by 7 Oct victims' families.
author: Guardian World

title: Triglav glacier disappears from Slovenia’s highest peak after scorching summer
content:
Slovenia’s highest peak, Triglav, has lost its remaining glacier, with the final ice patch disappearing after an exceptionally hot summer. Researchers noted that the ice mass had already shed 93 % of its surface area between 1983 and 2003, shrinking to less than a hectare of exposed rock, yet it persisted for two more decades before vanishing.

The loss is described as the latest Alpine casualty of Europe’s scorching summer, and the glacier’s disappearance is noted on a mountain regarded as a symbol of Slovenian identity.
summary: The final ice patch of Slovenia’s Triglav glacier on its highest peak has vanished after extreme heat accelerated its disappearance. The glacier lost 93% of its surface area between 1983 and 2003, shrinking to less than a hectare before persisting for two more decades.
author: Guardian World

title: Oleshky ceasefire holds as two European leaders have frank call with Putin
content:
A local ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky appeared to hold on Tuesday, with both sides halting drone attacks ahead of an evacuation for approximately 2,000 trapped civilians. The temporary truce began at 3am, marking the first time the frontline near the southern Ukrainian city has been quiet in years. Oleshky is located on the Dnipro River, roughly three miles from Kherson, which Ukrainian troops recaptured in autumn 2022.

Concurrently, two European leaders held a “frank” call with Vladimir Putin. The source does not provide further details regarding the specific leaders or the content of their discussion.
summary: Oleshky ceasefire holds as two European leaders have frank call with Putin.

content:

content:

A report by Metrópoles, citing people close to the politician’s family, said the senator was on a plane bound for the United States and had missed the deadline to hand over his passport. The outlet noted that the plane is in flight, though it did not specify the departure point.
